title: Zcash Developers Sound Alarm Over Privacy Pool Holding 400,000 ZEC
summary: Zcash developers urge holders to migrate 400,000 ZEC from Sapling to Ironwood amid speculative AI-driven cryptographic risks.
content:
Independent Zcash engineering team Zakura has called for accelerating the retirement of the network’s legacy Sapling shielded pool, where approximately 400,000 ZEC remains, amid speculation that artificial intelligence (AI)-driven mathematical breakthroughs could eventually compromise certain forms of pairing-based cryptography.

Key Takeaways

  • Approximately 400,000 ZEC, worth roughly $284 million, remains in Zcash’s legacy Sapling pool.
  • Zakura recommends disabling Sapling deposits and encouraging users to migrate to Ironwood.
  • ZEC fell roughly 4% to 6% Thursday, extending its monthly decline to approximately 46%.

Zakura Calls for Accelerated Retirement of Zcash’s Sapling Pool

On Thursday, Nov. 26, Zakura, an independent engineering initiative developing a Rust-based Zcash node client, published an extensive cryptographic risk assessment. Led by longtime Zcash cryptographer Sean Bowe and Osmosis co-founder Dev Ojha, the team addressed speculation surrounding integer factorization and its potential implications for blockchain security.

“The time to prepare for a cryptographic breakthrough is before it happens,” Zakura stated.

The discussion follows reports of a proof of the Riemann hypothesis and unsubstantiated rumors that AI laboratories have achieved breakthroughs in integer factorization, the mathematical problem underpinning RSA encryption. Although cryptocurrencies rarely employ RSA, related mathematical advances could have consequences for pairing-based cryptography.

Zakura maintained that neither Zcash’s transparent transactions nor Ironwood, its modern shielded pool, relies on factoring or cryptographic pairings. Sapling, however, employs pairings within its zero-knowledge proof (ZKP) system.

“In Zcash’s legacy Sapling pool, neither users’ private keys nor their note commitments rely on pairings. Only the proof system does. A pairing break enables an attacker to forge proofs, putting the 400,000 ZEC in Sapling at risk,” the developers explained.

The distinction is significant because compromised proofs would not necessarily render legitimate users’ funds permanently unrecoverable.

“Fortunately, Sapling’s proof system can be replaced without replacing its note commitments,” Zakura added.

The engineering team outlined a potential recovery mechanism involving freezing Sapling before its state becomes compromised and subsequently introducing an alternative proof system.

AI Breakthroughs Could Have Implications for Ethereum and Solana

Zakura emphasized that the potential vulnerability extends well beyond Zcash, noting that numerous blockchain networks employ pairing-based cryptography to authenticate consensus signatures.

“Blockchains using pairings for consensus would need to urgently migrate to alternative signature schemes,” the team said, identifying Ethereum, Solana and BNB among the networks potentially affected.

Nevertheless, the developers cautioned against mistaking mathematical speculation for an imminent security crisis.

“Practical pairing breaks are highly speculative. Still, our recommendation is to accelerate Sapling’s planned deprecation. This means that payments into Sapling should be disabled by a network upgrade.”

According to Zakura, fewer than 2.6% of Zcash transactions over the past 30 days involved Sapling, with known mining-related transfers accounting for 66% of that activity.

The team also estimated that even a hypothetical billionfold improvement in relevant attack techniques could leave the computational expense of breaking the underlying cryptography between $1 trillion and $300 trillion.

ZEC Slides as Developers Advocate Stronger Cryptographic Standards

Beyond retiring Sapling, Zakura advocated raising cryptographic security targets to 192-bit or 256-bit levels across blockchain ecosystems. The team is developing a proposal to integrate SPHINCS+ (SLH-DSA-192), a hash-based signature scheme designed to facilitate post-quantum transparent transactions.

“The AI math breakthroughs are likely not going to stop,” the developers warned.

Meanwhile, ZEC experienced considerable selling pressure on Thursday afternoon, exchanging hands between approximately $702 and $715 after recording an intraday low near $662. The privacy-focused cryptocurrency has shed roughly 22% to 23% over the past week, with its market capitalization hovering near $12 billion.

No evidence establishes that Zakura’s warning precipitated Thursday’s selling, particularly given ZEC’s prolonged November downturn.

For now, Zakura’s assessment presents a precautionary engineering challenge rather than a confirmed cryptographic emergency. The greater question facing cryptocurrency developers is whether protocol upgrades can keep pace with mathematical discoveries as AI compresses research timelines. Zcash’s proposed migration offers one example of preparing for that possibility before speculation becomes computational reality.

title: Galaxy Abandons BTC Bottom Call, Warns Bear Market Is Far From Over
summary: Galaxy Digital retracts its October bottom call, warning that bitcoin’s bear market isn't over after breaking below key 50- and 200-week MAs.
content:
Galaxy Digital’s research arm has retracted its earlier call that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June 2026, warning of continued downside risk.

Key Takeaways

  • Galaxy Digital retracted its Oct. 26 bottom thesis after bitcoin broke below its 50- and 200-week averages.
  • Eleven of Galaxy’s 13 bottom signals remain unmet, keeping market pressure firmly on crypto buyers.
  • A daily bitcoin close below $58,525 risks triggering another historical drawdown of at least 17%.

Moving-Average Breakdowns Invalidate October Thesis

Galaxy Digital’s research arm, led by Head of Firmwide Research Alex Thorn, has withdrawn its earlier view that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June 2026, warning that key technical breakdowns and unmet historical bottom signals point to ongoing downside risk.

In a new research note, Galaxy reversed its Oct. 26 thesis that investors should treat the summer downturn as finished.

“Our Oct. 26 note argued that bitcoin’s bear market ended in June. Its technical argument is no longer valid,” the firm wrote, noting that the technical foundation supporting a June bottom has eroded after bitcoin (BTC) surrendered major trend lines and slipped back toward its summer lows.

Galaxy’s case that the bear market remains active rests on technical breakdowns, proximity to summer lows, and a shortage of historical bottom signals. The firm’s earlier October outlook had leaned heavily on bitcoin reclaiming its 50-week moving average for seven consecutive weekly closes.

Unmet Bottom Signals and Downside Risk

However, the note states that “after seven weekly closes above the 50-week average, bitcoin closed back below it in the week ended Nov. 8 and closed the following week below the 200-week average,” invalidating the breakout signal. Those moving-average failures coincided with a renewed test of bitcoin’s summer troughs.

“On Nov. 20, BTC traded below its July 1 intraday low, reaching $55,100 on Nov. 21,” Galaxy wrote. Even after rebounding to close at $61,104 on Nov. 22, “the June 30 closing low of $58,525 was intact by just 4.4%,” leaving the cryptocurrency perilously close to a fresh breakdown.

Beyond price action, Galaxy noted that 11 of the 13 historical bottom indicators in its tracking framework remain unfulfilled, leaving only two signals met and placing the burden of proof firmly back on buyers. Historically, Galaxy added, prior breakdowns below established bear-market lows have been followed by further declines of at least 17%, raising the risk of a steeper leg down if the $58,525 closing level gives way on a daily basis.

For Galaxy’s earlier constructive case to regain traction, Thorn noted that bitcoin would need to recover back above both the 200-week and 50-week moving averages on a weekly closing basis. Until those trend lines are reclaimed and more bottom signals flash green, Galaxy’s research frames the broader market as still contending with bear-market pressure.

title: US House Panel Advances Bitcoin Reserve Bill With 20-Year Holding Rule
summary: A US House committee advanced a bill to put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and bar sales of Bitcoin held in it for at least 20 years.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

A US House committee advanced a bill to put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and bar sales of Bitcoin held in it for at least 20 years.

The US House Financial Services Committee has advanced a bill that would put the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law and require the Treasury to hold Bitcoin deposited in it for at least 20 years from enactment.

The committee reported H.R. 8957, the American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, with amendments on November 24. The bill was placed on the House Union Calendar, a step that makes it eligible for floor consideration. It still needs to clear the House and Senate and be signed into law. Alaska Republican Rep. Nick Begich introduced the measure in May.

What Treasury could do with the reserve

The bill would direct qualifying Bitcoin already owned by the federal government into the reserve and qualifying non-Bitcoin assets into a separate Digital Asset Stockpile. Treasury would administer both. The bill says reserve assets could not be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of” during the minimum holding period. The restriction starts on the date the law takes effect and applies to Bitcoin acquired by the US and deposited in the reserve, regardless of how the government obtained it.

Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to recommend whether to keep holding the Bitcoin or allow a gradual release. Once the period expires, the secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve’s assets in any two-year period.

The bill separately gives Treasury a year from enactment to study when an early sale might be appropriate and recommend any changes to the law, including possible exceptions for national security or financial stability. That study would leave any decision to create an exception with Congress.

How it builds on the 2025 executive order

President Donald Trump established the reserve and stockpile by executive order in March 2025. The order used eligible forfeited Bitcoin as the basis for the reserve and directed the government to retain Bitcoin deposited in it. It also authorised Treasury and Commerce to develop strategies to acquire additional Bitcoin without imposing incremental costs on taxpayers.

The House bill would set the holding rule in statute and create reporting and public proof-of-reserves requirements. It would also give Treasury and Commerce 180 days to study whether the government could acquire more Bitcoin in a way that avoids increasing the national debt. The bill calls for a study and sets no purchase target or acquisition schedule. A separate proposal from Sen. Cynthia Lummis would authorise the government to acquire an additional one million Bitcoin.

The next step is a House floor vote. The Block reported that the approaching end of the 119th Congress leaves limited time for both chambers to act.

title: ‘Very racist’ Netflix SBF series, BitMart’s $319M shortfall: Asia Express
summary: Netflix’s The Altruist has been slammed for its ‘very racist’ portrayal of CZ. BitMart reportedly has a $319.5 million shortfall and just $1.9M in liquid assets.
content:
Ex-FTX COO calls out Netflix over CZ’s ‘Asian mafia’ portrayal

Former FTX chief operating officer Constance Waing has slammed Netflix’s portrayal of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in The Altruists as racist, saying it relied on Asian mafia stereotypes.

“It’s very racist,” Waing told Cointelegraph. The Altruists is a dramatization of the rise and fall of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX crypto empire and his subsequent imprisonment for fraud.

Waing took issue with one scene in which FTX founder SBF and Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison enter through a back door to meet CZ, saying it suggested he was “trying to get these two innocent people into something bad.”

In another episode the fictional CZ urges SBF to give Alameda Research advance access to FTX customer orders so it can trade ahead of them, a suggestion the real CZ labelled “insane.” Ethereum creator Vitalik Buterin said the portrayal exaggerated Zhao’s accent and questioned whether it was racist.

Woke 1 may have been crazy, but racist is still racist says Vitalik Buterin.

SOUTH KOREA

South Korean exchanges halt CYBER transfers amid suspected bridge exploit

South Korean crypto exchanges Upbit and Bithumb suspended deposits and withdrawals of CYBER on Sunday after the project reported suspicious activity involving its cross-chain bridge.

On Saturday, Cyber said it detected unexpected minting of CYBER tokens on Solana, followed by a transfer of tokens out of its bridge’s Ethereum lockbox. Cyber, formerly CyberConnect, operates an Ethereum layer-2 network designed for social applications.

The project said it was investigating the incident and advised users to avoid using the bridge or depositing CYBER to exchanges while the investigation continues.

South Korea proposes bank-led stablecoins, 20% cap on crypto exchange stakes

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled a draft bill Tuesday that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to groups majority-owned by banks and generally cap shareholders’ stakes in crypto exchanges at 20%.

The draft also seeks to lift South Korea’s 2017 ban on domestic initial coin offerings.

The 20% ownership rule is set to affect a deal that Naver struck for Upbit owner Dunamu. The deal gave Naver full control, but under the new rules shares above the 20% cap would lose their vote.

South Korea’s crypto bill could move stablecoin race beyond token issuance

South Korean fintech companies could gain influence in bank-led stablecoin groups by signing up partners that help people spend won-denominated tokens, Tiger Research said in its Tuesday report.

“Those relationships are likely to matter more to the business than the volume of stablecoins issued,” the Asia-focused research company said.

NORTH KOREA

US seeks to recover $1.1B in crypto stolen in North Korea-linked Binance hack

The US Department of Justice is seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in crypto stolen from cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October by North Korean hackers.

In a court filing Monday, prosecutors asked a federal court in Washington, DC, to permanently forfeit the funds, which are held in the USDC stablecoin. Since the attack, US authorities said they have helped to freeze, seize or return nearly $3 billion of the more than $6 billion taken from Binance.

JAPAN

Japan’s SBI, SMFG launch Solana venture for stablecoins, tokenization

Japanese financial giants SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) have launched a joint venture with the Solana Foundation to tokenize assets, develop stablecoin payment infrastructure and expand onchain financial services across Asia.

More news from Japan

Japan’s Financial Services Agency has published briefing materials considering proposals to regulate apps and sites that connect to DeFi, and whether to discourage access to protocols that lack money laundering controls.

Daiwa has completed a technical verification in which AI agents processed natural language instructions to screen various DEX options and to conduct stablecoin and security token swaps.

HONG KONG

Source: Pexels

Hong Kong launches tokenized debt platform with 24-hour settlement

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched a platform Wednesday that supports round-the-clock settlement of tokenized debt securities in multiple currencies.

The CMU Digital Asset Platform, developed and operated by CMU OmniClear Limited on behalf of the HKMA, uses cash tokens for payment and connects with conventional payment systems and central bank digital currencies.

HK pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules

Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration.

On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing that firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from, or register with, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC). The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.

More news from Hong Kong

BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Hong Kong and the Asia-Pacific region. It allows investors to use new HK stablecoin HKDAP to subscribe and redeem from the fund which offers a constant net asset value.

SINGAPORE

The Monetary Authority of Singapore has clarified that an on-chain token is not automatically a bank deposit. It draws a line between genuine tokenized deposits and crypto-like bearer instruments.

A UK court has approved an asset recovery settlement totaling 55 million pounds from Su Haijin and Xu Haika, two defendants in Singapore’s largest money-laundering case. Haika is being forced to sell 16 London apartments held through affiliated companies to repay the funds. The August 2023 police operation saw crypto worth more than S$38 million seized.

CHINA

According to Nikkei Asia, Bitmart has a $319.5 million shortfall but just $1.9 million in liquid assets available for customer repayments. Numerous users report they have been unable to access their accounts.

Bitmart disclosed the figures to Alvarez & Marsal, which is overseeing the restructuring process. The collapse highlights the dangers of high yield crypto products, with Chinese investors reportedly drawn to the platform by short term savings products offering 18.8% annualized yields for 14 day deposits.

title: DeFi Giant Sky Proposes $25M Liquidity Lifeline for Stranded stUSDS Depositors
summary: Sky proposes an emergency $25M USDS transfer as co-founder Rune Christensen's $77 million debt contributes to the stUSDS liquidity crisis.
content:
Decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol Sky, formerly Makerdao, has proposed an emergency transfer of 25 million USDS to alleviate a lending pool liquidity crisis that has persisted for more than two weeks, with co-founder Rune Christensen acknowledging a role in the predicament.

Key Takeaways

  • Sky proposed an emergency 25 million USDS transfer to facilitate debt repayments and restore stUSDS liquidity.
  • Christensen acknowledged owing approximately 77 million USDS, with his borrowing contributing to withdrawal restrictions.
  • Data shows stUSDS withdrawals peaked last week.

Sky Seeks Emergency Intervention as Lending Pool Runs Dry

Sky’s governance apparatus is pursuing an unscheduled executive vote to transfer 25 million of the stablecoin USDS to the Sky Frontier Foundation, accelerating a previously planned capital allocation intended to facilitate debt repayment and release liquidity for depositors.

The funds were originally earmarked for the foundation but omitted from the Nov. 19 executive vote. Approximately 6 million USDS would come from Amatsu, 4 million from Ozone and 15 million from the Core Council Executive Agent 1 (CCEA1).

Sky’s core facilitators determined that waiting until the next scheduled executive vote on Dec. 3 would prolong the liquidity crunch unnecessarily.

The stUSDS product allows depositors to earn variable yields by supplying capital for loans collateralized by staked SKY tokens. However, when borrowers consume virtually all available capital, depositors must rely on fresh deposits or debt repayments to withdraw their funds.

According to an analysis by blockchain analytics firm Bitquery, daily withdrawals approached $14 million two weeks ago, draining available liquidity. Subsequent Spark data showed utilization hovering near 100%, effectively leaving depositors stranded despite the pool holding substantial assets.

Sky Co-Founder Admits Borrowing Was a ‘Big Mistake’

On Nov. 23, Christensen disclosed that he had repaid 3 million USDS but still owed approximately 77 million USDS against his staked SKY holdings. Bitquery’s analysis attributed roughly 48% of the pool’s outstanding debt to a wallet associated with the co-founder.

Christensen characterized his borrowing strategy as “a big mistake,” acknowledging that he had underestimated the potential for borrowing rates to climb. He apologized and indicated that he was exploring direct SKY sales to institutional investors.

“To repay the rest, I’m exploring options to sell part of my SKY directly to institutional investors who share Sky’s vision of becoming infrastructure that institutions can rely on,” Christensen added.

Complicating matters, existing governance parameters had disabled liquidations on the SKY-backed positions, limiting the protocol’s ability to forcibly unwind loans.

Meanwhile, South Korean cryptocurrency exchanges Upbit, Bithumb and Coinone placed SKY and USDS on trading warning lists and suspended deposits. USDS nevertheless maintained its dollar peg, distinguishing the lending pool’s liquidity constraints from the stablecoin’s broader stability.

Alternative community proposals include deploying $40 million to $50 million in reserves to purchase SKY directly from borrowers, with the proceeds simultaneously directed toward debt repayments. Other suggestions involve reducing borrowing rates and suspending new loans.

As of Nov. 26, the emergency transfer remains a proposal rather than a completed intervention. Even if approved, the allocation does not guarantee unrestricted withdrawals. The DeFi platform Sky‘s predicament illustrates a fundamental vulnerability in collateralized defi lending: A pool can hold considerable assets on paper while offering depositors virtually no immediate access to their capital.

title: BNB Chain details new layer-1 for trading, private finance and AI
summary: The proposed network will operate alongside BNB Smart Chain and retain BNB as its native token, with a public testnet targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
content:
BNB Chain has outlined plans for a new layer-1 blockchain designed to support high-frequency trading, payments, private financial transactions and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents.

According to a litepaper published Thursday, the network would operate alongside the existing BNB Smart Chain (BSC) and use BNB as its native token, with no new native token planned. The blockchain is currently running as a development network, with BNB Chain targeting a public testnet launch in the first quarter of 2027 and a mainnet launch in the second half of the year.

On general-purpose blockchains, applications typically compete for block space. The proposed network would reserve a portion of its transaction capacity for specific activities, such as payments services, which BNB Chain said could reduce competition for network resources during periods of high demand.

The proposed network would also feature an optional shielded pool designed to support private transfers involving BNB and other supported tokens, including certain decentralized finance (DeFi) transactions. Some transaction details would remain publicly visible, and BNB Chain’s documentation warns that the pool’s circuits remain unaudited and that it should not be used with real funds.

Other proposed features would allow users to transact without first acquiring BNB to pay network fees and authorize AI agents to execute transactions within predefined limits.

title: Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack
summary: The announcement concludes a phased withdrawal recovery that began on Nov. 1, when Binance restored Bitcoin withdrawals following the record crypto theft.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 26, 2026

The announcement concludes a phased withdrawal recovery that began on Nov. 1, when Binance restored Bitcoin withdrawals following the record crypto theft.

Binance said Thursday it had lifted all withdrawal suspensions related to its October hack, four weeks after an attack drained $6.3 billion in funds from the exchange in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.

In an announcement, Binance said withdrawals had resumed across nearly all networks, with a small number remaining temporarily suspended due to maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.

The exchange’s network status page shows partial deposit and withdrawal suspensions for several cryptocurrencies. USDC withdrawals, for instance, remain suspended on Hedera and World Chain due to low hot wallet balances and on Sonic due to security issues.

Binance warned users against phishing attempts, saying it would never request passwords or seed phrases or offer expedited withdrawals. The exchange also said customers could verify that their assets are backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 through its proof-of-reserves system.

The Oct. 29 attack targeted Binance’s hot wallets across multiple blockchains, with blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributing the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Following the breach, Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses.

Thursday’s announcement marks the end of a phased recovery process that began on Nov. 1, when Binance resumed Bitcoin (BTC) withdrawals before gradually restoring services across other blockchain networks.

title: UK is ‘getting it wrong’ on DeFi regulation, says Coinbase
summary: Coinbase and Stand With Crypto argue that the FCA’s proposed DeFi rules could leave UK users without regulated access to decentralized finance.
content:
Coinbase and Stand With Crypto, a crypto advocacy group backed by the exchange, are pushing back against the UK’s proposed approach to decentralized finance (DeFi), arguing that restrictions on regulated crypto platforms could leave consumers with fewer safeguards when accessing DeFi services.

The criticism follows reports on Nov. 26 that the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) plans to proceed with tighter rules and authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing money laundering risks exposed by the $6.3 billion Binance hack. Although the attack targeted a centralized exchange, hackers moved stolen funds through decentralized protocols, complicating efforts to trace and freeze the assets.

Katie Harries, head of policy for Europe at Coinbase, said the proposals could limit opportunities for regulated firms to work with authorities on consumer safeguards.

“The UK is getting its approach to DeFi wrong,” Harries told Cointelegraph. “This isn’t a ban on UK consumers using DeFi; it’s a ban on giving them a regulated route to use it.”

In an October opinion piece for Cointelegraph, Harries argued that the proposed framework could effectively prevent regulated crypto platforms from offering DeFi services, as requirements to execute customer orders through authorized trading venues could exclude decentralized protocols with no central operator capable of obtaining FCA authorization.

Related: Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets

UK users could face fewer DeFi options

Harries argued that regulated platforms could help address the FCA’s concerns around DeFi through due diligence and safeguards.

The FCA has previously used regulatory sandboxes to allow financial services firms to test new products in live markets under regulatory oversight. On Feb. 25, the regulator named four regulated entities to test out stablecoin products within its regulatory sandbox.

“The UK has got a lot right on crypto, but its approach is closing the door on DeFi innovation,” Harries said.

Harry Pearce-Gould, general manager at Stand With Crypto, argued that the proposals could leave UK users with fewer options for accessing DeFi services. “That leaves UK crypto users without the trusted, regulated routes to access DeFi that will be available to people doing the same thing in other jurisdictions.”

He said people should be able to use crypto for financial activities such as borrowing against their holdings, provided they have clear information about the associated risks.

UK’s ambitions as a global crypto hub

The implications could extend beyond consumer protection, potentially putting the UK at a competitive disadvantage in the digital asset industry, according to Harries. “The UK is creating a prohibition, and that doesn’t sit right with its ambition to be a global centre for digital assets,” she said.

The FCA closed consultations on its proposed DeFi guidance and wider crypto regulatory framework on Nov. 18, with final guidance expected in January 2027. The new regime is scheduled to take effect on Oct. 25, 2027.

title: Freeze First, Court Later: Spain Lets AML Unit Halt Crypto Accounts Without a Judge
summary:
Spain’s financial intelligence unit will soon be able to freeze crypto asset accounts for up to five business days, and block individual transfers for up to ten without waiting for a court order.
Under Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, published on 25 November, Spanish anti-money laundering watchdog Sepblac...
content:
2026-11-26T22:35:47.918+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 20:35 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Sepblac will be able to freeze cryptoasset, bank and payment accounts for up to five business days while investigating suspected money laundering or terrorist financing.
  • Crypto platforms must execute and lift these temporary orders within the statutory deadlines, with non-compliance classified as a very serious infringement.

Spain’s financial intelligence unit will soon be able to freeze crypto asset accounts for up to five business days, and block individual transfers for up to ten without waiting for a court order.

Under Royal Decree-Law 44/2026, published on 25 November, Spanish anti-money laundering watchdog Sepblac is granted direct authority to lock down digital asset accounts along with traditional bank and payment accounts. Judicial oversight only required if prosecutors seek to extend a freeze beyond the initial statutory window.

However, the decree-law remains provisional until Spain’s Congress validates or rejects it within 30 days of its adoption.

Accounts and Individual Transactions Have Different Limits

The new Article 46 bis allows Sepblac, Spain’s financial intelligence unit, to suspend the use of a bank, payment or cryptoasset account when it finds indications that the account may be connected to money laundering or terrorist financing.

It can also suspend the broader business relationship between a customer and a financial services provider. An account or business-relationship restriction can remain in place for a maximum of five business days.

A separate limit applies to an individual transaction already in progress: Sepblac can stop or refuse it for up to ten business days. Both measures must end earlier if Sepblac determines that they are no longer necessary.

Once the relevant deadline expires, the restriction automatically lapses unless a court ratifies or extends it following a request submitted by a public prosecutor before the deadline.

Sepblac can issue the initial order itself, while the judicial involvement becomes necessary if authorities want to keep the restriction in place beyond the statutory limit.

Crypto Platforms Must Be Able to Execute the Orders

Cryptoasset service providers already fall within the group of businesses subject to Spain’s main AML law.

The amendment gives this existing obligation a more immediate operational consequence: covered platforms must be able to execute and subsequently lift Sepblac orders within the applicable five- or ten-day window.

Failure to comply with a suspension order will be classified as a very serious infringement. The decree also protects firms from liability when they restrict an account or transaction in accordance with Sepblac’s instructions.

The Spanish government linked the change to Financial Action Task Force standards requiring financial intelligence units to have effective powers to stop suspicious transactions.

Sepblac may also use the mechanism at the request of Spanish law enforcement or another financial intelligence unit in the EU or a third country, extending its relevance to cross-border investigations.

title: Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Plunges $6 Billion: The Cost of His Bitcoin Bet
summary: Key takeaways Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes. The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales. Saylor’...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Michael Saylor’s estimated net worth has fallen about $6 billion, from $9.3 billion in October 2025 to roughly $3.3 billion on November 25, 2026, a 64.5% drop per Forbes.
  • The $6 billion is a drop in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any asset sales.
  • Saylor’s personal 17,732 BTC (bought for about $175 million) would be worth roughly $1.07 billion at $60,325, assuming he still holds them all.
  • Strategy holds 851,305 BTC bought at an average $75,446, leaving a paper shortfall of about $12.88 billion against its $64.23 billion cost.
  • Strategy’s mNAV was 0.94 at the November 25 close, so raising capital by issuing shares has become harder, and that matters as much as the Bitcoin price.

Michael Saylor’s net worth has fallen by approximately $6 billion since the cryptocurrency market peaked in October 2025. The Strategy co-founder, whose fortune was estimated at $9.3 billion at the time, is now worth around $3.3 billion, according to Forbes.

The decline has wiped out nearly two-thirds of Saylor’s estimated wealth. Yet the billionaire’s company continues to accumulate Bitcoin despite mounting paper losses, showing little willingness to reconsider its investment strategy.

For Saylor, the downturn presents a problem that extends well beyond the price of Bitcoin. Much of his fortune depends on a company that must convince investors to keep financing its accumulation strategy.

How Much Has Michael Saylor Lost During the Bitcoin Crash?

Saylor was already among the cryptocurrency industry’s biggest financial casualties in February, when Forbes estimated that his wealth had fallen by $4.7 billion from its October 2025 level.

His fortune briefly stabilized in the following months, reaching an estimated $4.7 billion in June, before suffering another setback.

The latest estimate puts Saylor’s wealth approximately 64.5% below its October 2025 level.

Source: Forbes. Selected valuation snapshots, not daily observations. Hover over a bar for details.

Bitcoin’s return to the $60,000 level has added pressure, but the cryptocurrency alone does not explain the scale of the decline. Saylor’s exposure through Strategy makes his financial position considerably more complicated than that of an ordinary Bitcoin investor.

The $6 billion represents a reduction in estimated wealth, not a confirmed cash loss or the proceeds of any disclosed asset sales.

How Much Bitcoin Does Michael Saylor Personally Own?

In October 2020, Saylor disclosed that he personally owned 17,732 BTC, acquired for approximately $175 million.

At the Bitcoin price of $60,325 reported by Strategy on November 26, those holdings would be worth approximately $1.07 billion, assuming he still owns the entire disclosed amount.

That would leave his original personal investment with an unrealized gain of roughly $895 million.

His current personal Bitcoin balance has not been independently confirmed, but the calculation illustrates an important distinction. Saylor can lose billions in estimated wealth while remaining substantially profitable on his original Bitcoin purchases.

The situation at Strategy is quite different.

Strategy Is Sitting on Nearly $13 Billion in Bitcoin Paper Losses

While Saylor began buying Bitcoin at considerably lower prices, his company has spent much of the past several years increasing its exposure at higher valuations.

According to its November 23 SEC filing, Strategy acquired another 457 BTC for $29.6 million, bringing its total holdings to 851,305 BTC.

The company has spent approximately $64.23 billion accumulating Bitcoin at an average purchase price of $75,446.

Its official Bitcoin dashboard valued those reserves at approximately $51.35 billion on November 26.

That leaves a gap of nearly $12.9 billion between the company’s cumulative acquisition cost and the market value of its Bitcoin holdings.

Strategy Bitcoin portfolio Value
Total holdings 851,305 BTC
Average acquisition price $75,446
Total acquisition cost $64.23 billion
Current Bitcoin reserve value $51.35 billion
Estimated shortfall against cost $12.88 billion

These figures do not represent realized trading losses, nor do they capture the full financial performance of the company.

Nevertheless, the numbers reveal how dramatically the economics of accumulating Bitcoin have changed during the downturn.

Why Saylor’s Fortune Is Vulnerable to More Than Bitcoin

For years, investors were willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares. The attraction was not simply the Bitcoin it owned, but the prospect that management could raise additional capital and increase shareholders’ exposure to the cryptocurrency.

That premium is no longer something the company can take for granted.

Strategy’s dashboard showed an mNAV ratio of 0.94 at the November 25 stock market close, using its own net Bitcoin value per share methodology.

The company’s latest investor briefing acknowledges the implications:

“

A widening discount can cause MSTR to underperform BTC even when bitcoin rises.

Strategy · Investor briefing

This is where Saylor’s investment model faces a more difficult test.

When investors are willing to pay a premium for Strategy shares, raising capital to acquire more Bitcoin can improve the economics of the business. When that premium disappears, issuing additional shares becomes a more complicated proposition.

Strategy’s own sensitivity analysis shows that a Bitcoin price of $40,000 would reduce its estimated net reserve value per share to $45.37, compared with $163.17 at a Bitcoin price of $100,000. The figures illustrate how sensitive the company’s underlying reserve valuation is to Bitcoin price movements.

Strategy’s third-quarter financial results offer a clearer picture of why its cash reserves and financing obligations now matter almost as much as the price of Bitcoin.

Buying more Bitcoin is only one part of the equation. The cost of financing those purchases matters just as much.

Could Michael Saylor’s Net Worth Recover?

There is a credible case for recovery. Strategy still owns more than 850,000 Bitcoin, giving it considerable exposure to any sustained cryptocurrency market rebound.

The company also reported approximately $4.82 billion in combined cash and dollar reserves in its latest investor briefing, providing a buffer against its financing obligations.

But a recovery in Bitcoin would not necessarily produce an equivalent recovery in Saylor’s wealth. Strategy’s share price also depends on its debt, preferred-stock obligations, access to capital and the valuation investors are willing to assign to its business model.

The next test for Saylor is not whether he can buy another thousand Bitcoin. It is whether he can continue financing those purchases on terms that benefit existing shareholders.

His personal fortune has already demonstrated how expensive that distinction can become.

title: GTA VI Is Now a Spectator Sport. Of Course You Can Bet on It
summary: Polymarket logged about $131,000 in trading on when a Twitch streamer would finish GTA VI. Vice City has acquired a betting desk, and the man at the centre of it is playing a video game.
content:
Skip to content

Polymarket logged about $131,000 in trading on when a Twitch streamer would finish GTA VI. Vice City has acquired a betting desk, and the man at the centre of it is playing a video game.

I thought the most Vice City thing you could do this week was drive a stolen car into the ocean and blame the handling. It turns out you can sit at home and take a financial position on when a man called TheBurntPeanut will finish Grand Theft Auto VI. The ocean can wait.

Polymarket displayed about US$131,000 in trading volume on its TheBurntPeanut finish-date market. That’s the value of trades, and the same shares can change hands more than once. Still, it’s a substantial amount of buying and selling over the question of when one Twitch streamer will be done with a video game.

Polymarket’s GTA VI page also lists contracts on when another streamer, ohnePixel, would finish and when Rockstar might release a PC version. The PC one I get. Millions of people would like a date from a company perfectly happy to let them keep asking. The Peanut one is more interesting because nearly everything that makes him worth watching can also make him take longer.

Please proceed directly to the plot

Rockstar spent years building a world in which wandering off is half the pleasure. Some of the best moments in these games start when you miss a turn, hear something good on the radio or decide, on evidence available only to you, that a particular car needs to be in a particular swimming pool. A deadline contract gives somebody watching at home a reason to look at that same swimming pool and think about the time.

Polymarket lists TheBurntPeanut’s Twitch channel as a resolution source. Its contract titles use the word “by,” which matters. Several dates can resolve Yes if he finishes early enough. The deadlines are separate propositions. For the viewer, the difference between finishing a game and continuing to play it is pleasantly blurry. For anybody settling a contract, it has to be sharp enough to pay out on.

Imagine buying Yes on a near deadline and then watching him discover a boat. Before you placed the bet, the boat was good television. You might even have been the person in chat demanding he steal it. Now you have the unfortunate experience of sincerely wanting a man in a video game to ignore a boat. You could have had that feeling for free by becoming somebody’s project manager.

The audience has a position

Sports betting already taught people to watch the last few minutes of a decided game because somebody still needs to score. A streamer’s schedule gives a market looser material. A broadcast can run late, stop early or turn into forty minutes of something the person playing finds hilarious. He’s also close enough to his viewers to read what they type. You can see the potential for a very strange chat window when some of the people in it would prefer he keep moving.

That’s a possibility, and the trading volume tells us about trades. It can’t tell us how a streamer played or why a particular viewer kept watching. The reason this market is worth a look is how cheaply it can change the stakes for the audience. A running joke, a detour, or a decision to call it a night can suddenly have a financial meaning for someone who has absolutely no say in any of it.

I wrote last week about how much ownership you get when you buy GTA VI. There is now a pleasantly absurd alternative. You can buy an interest in how quickly somebody else gets through his copy. I hope he takes the boat.

title: Monero’s Delisting Nightmare Continues: XMR Price Plunges 15%
summary: Key takeaways Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR. KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31. XMR will also stop b...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Monero fell about 15% on Thursday, from $525.36 to $446.54 per BitInfoCharts, after KuCoin announced it will delist XMR.
  • KuCoin will end all four XMR spot pairs on November 30 at 08:00 UTC; deposits are already suspended and withdrawals stay open until December 31.
  • XMR will also stop being accepted as collateral for VIP loans, so borrowers may need to add other collateral to avoid liquidation.
  • KuCoin is the most active XMR venue (about $62.6 million in 24-hour volume on XMR/USDT per CoinGecko), following MEXC, Binance and Kraken EEA exits.
  • The network does not depend on KuCoin, but liquidity does: watch where volume migrates and how much slippage the remaining exchanges show.

Monero (XMR) lost around 15% of its value in less than five hours on Thursday after KuCoin announced plans to remove the privacy coin from its platform. The decision comes just nine days after rival exchange MEXC discontinued XMR spot trading, leaving investors with fewer options to trade one of the cryptocurrency market’s largest privacy-focused assets.

Data from BitInfoCharts shows that Monero fell from $525.36 to $446.54 during Thursday’s trading session. For longtime XMR investors, the sell-off is an uncomfortable reminder of what happened when Binance announced its Monero delisting in February 2024.

This time, however, the list of major exchanges available to Monero traders is considerably shorter.

KuCoin Gives Monero Traders Four Days Before Trading Ends

In a November 26 announcement, KuCoin confirmed that it will remove all four Monero spot trading pairs against USDT, USDC, ETH and BTC on November 30 at 08:00 UTC.

The exchange has already suspended XMR deposits and does not intend to reopen them. Withdrawals are scheduled to remain available until December 31 at 08:00 UTC, although KuCoin reserves the right to close them earlier if problems affecting the network arise.

Monero’s removal extends beyond spot trading. KuCoin will discontinue XMR flexible savings on November 27, followed by its conversion and automated trading services on November 30.

There is another detail in the announcement that deserves particular attention. KuCoin will stop accepting XMR as collateral for its VIP loan products. Customers who have borrowed against their Monero holdings may need to provide alternative collateral to avoid liquidation.

For holders planning to leave their coins on the exchange until the withdrawal deadline, KuCoin also warned that remaining balances could be converted into stablecoins, although “such conversion is not guaranteed.”

The exchange cited its platform policies but did not identify a specific regulatory requirement behind the decision.

Monero’s Liquidity Problem Is Getting Harder To Ignore

KuCoin is not the first exchange to abandon Monero this month, but its departure could prove particularly significant given the amount of XMR trading it handles.

A November 26 snapshot from CoinGecko identified KuCoin as Monero’s most active exchange, with its XMR/USDT pair recording approximately $62.6 million in trading volume over a 24-hour period.

Earlier this month, MEXC discontinued spot trading for Monero on November 17. Binance removed the cryptocurrency in February 2024, while Kraken halted XMR trading for European Economic Area customers in October of the same year, explicitly citing regulatory changes.

Kaiko’s historical research illustrates how liquidity across privacy cryptocurrencies had already deteriorated by early 2024, following a series of exchange restrictions.

Trading volume does not simply disappear when an exchange delists an asset. Some of it will move elsewhere, and investors who intend to keep their holdings can withdraw them to private wallets.

The bigger question is how efficiently the remaining exchanges can absorb that activity. If fewer venues are competing for the same orders, particularly during periods of market stress, large trades could become more expensive to execute and price swings more pronounced.

For Monero, that is increasingly a market structure problem rather than a question of whether its underlying technology works.

Can XMR Survive Another Major Exchange Exit?

There is a case against assuming that Thursday’s sell-off marks the beginning of a prolonged decline.

Monero has survived previous exchange removals and even managed to establish new price highs in 2026 despite mounting restrictions. As NewsBTC previously reported, XMR traded above $700 earlier this year, long after Binance stopped supporting its spot markets.

The cryptocurrency’s network does not depend on KuCoin to process transactions. Its utility as a privacy-focused payment system remains separate from its availability on centralized trading platforms.

But a functioning network does not guarantee a liquid market. Investors still need practical ways to enter and exit their positions without incurring excessive trading costs.

November 30 will therefore be an important test for Monero. Rather than focusing solely on whether XMR recovers the $500 level, traders should watch where KuCoin’s trading volume migrates and whether the remaining exchanges can absorb larger orders without substantial slippage.

That will offer a better indication of whether Thursday’s decline was a temporary reaction to another delisting or a warning of a deeper liquidity problem.

title: CMC Markets Profit More Than Doubles, but Shares Fall 11%
summary:
CMC Markets shares closed almost 11% lower on Thursday despite the broker reporting a record first half and more than doubling its pre-tax profit. 
The stock opened at 663 pence and initially climbed to 677 pence before reversing course. It finished at the session low of 580 pence, down 10.77% from ...
content:
2026-11-26T20:10:02.781+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 18:10 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • The stock reversed from an intraday high of 677 pence to close at the session low.
  • CMC reiterated the guidance that triggered a 23% rally in July.

CMC Markets shares closed almost 11% lower on Thursday despite the broker reporting a record first half and more than doubling its pre-tax profit.

The stock opened at 663 pence and initially climbed to 677 pence before reversing course. It finished at the session low of 580 pence, down 10.77% from the previous close of 650 pence.

Trading activity was also unusually high. About 2.56 million shares changed hands, more than ten times the 242,646 recorded during the previous session.

Same Forecast, Different Market Reaction

The financial results, including the profit increase and CMC’s entry on the UK crypto asset register, were covered separately by Finance Magnates. For the market reaction, the more relevant detail is that CMC reiterated its previously upgraded FY2027 guidance.

The broker continues to expect at least £550 million in net operating income and £250 million in EBITDA, but it did not raise those targets again.

When CMC introduced the same forecast in July, its shares jumped 23% to what was then a record high of around 570 pence. Thursday’s announcement confirmed that outlook rather than changing it.

The contrast does not prove that the absence of another upgrade caused the decline, but it distinguishes the two announcements.

Shares Remain Above Their Annual Low

The fall followed a substantial earlier revaluation of CMC. The shares traded between 281 and 785 pence over the past 52 weeks. Thursday’s close was therefore still more than twice the annual low, although it left the stock roughly a quarter below its high.

CMC did not issue a separate statement about the decline. Its next scheduled financial update is the FY2027 results, expected in June 2027.

  • An early investor in Ethereum sold off the remaining 45,000 ETH for about $75.35 million.
  • The wallet originally acquired 100,000 ETH for around $31,000 in 2015.
  • Total proceeds from three separate sales were nearly $87.21 million.

A whale from early-time donor rounds in Ethereum has completely shifted from its stake by selling out its remaining 45,000 ETH holding. The last transaction, totaled at $75.35 million, adds up to a total investment of about $87.21 million, from $31,000 to the present.

  • Ethereum ICO Whale Completes Its Final ETH Sale
  • Three Transactions Generated $87.21 Million
    • A Decade-Long Exit Across Three Sales
    • Early Ethereum Holdings Continue to Attract Attention

Ethereum ICO Whale Completes Its Final ETH Sale

Cointelegraph highlighted the transaction in a November 26 post on X, reporting that the early investor had sold all remaining 45,000 ETH.

Its wallet had bought 100,000 ETH around the $31,000 mark during the 2015 fundraising round for the Ethereum network. This meant the initial transaction cost was about $0.31 per ETH.

With the latest sale, its entire balance of remaining assets sold. On average, it has been sold for about $1,674 per token, equaling nearly $75.35 million in total. Here, the address has sold off all of the 100,000 ETH originally allocated to it, meaning it no longer is in possession of any part of that allocation.

Three Transactions Generated $87.21 Million

The investor sold the total allotment in stages. Rather, the wallet spread its holdings out in three transactions spread across a couple of years and at vastly different sale prices.

A Decade-Long Exit Across Three Sales

The wallet sold 50,000 ETH at an average price of $5.47 in 2016, receiving approximately $274,000. In October 2026, it sold another 5,000 ETH at an average price of $2,316, generating roughly $11.58 million. The last one was on November 26, 2026, with the investor selling the remaining 45,000 ETH at about $1,674 each, adding $75.35 million.

These transactions, combined, generated about $87.21 million of proceeds on the initial investment of $31,000.

These are not actual net-profit numbers, but rather reported values in the three sales. They also detail a portion of the investor’s holding where he kept it in the allocation for years prior to exiting.

Read More: BitMine Adds 7,653 ETH as Treasury Nears 5% of Ethereum Supply After Sharp Price Rout

Early Ethereum Holdings Continue to Attract Attention

The sale of ETH from Ethereum’s initial fundraising round is a testament to the incredible returns some participants have seen for investing in cryptocurrency.

When we report buying it at the price it was sold, the wallet’s initial assignment of 100k ETH was only $31,000. Despite an average selling price of only $5.47 when the investor sold half of the stock in 2016, its eventual sales made her millions of dollars.

It also closed at a lower average price than the wallet did the previous October, when it traded 5,000 ETH for $2,316 per each. But much more of the latest disposal was in, so the bulk of the reported lifetime proceeds.

The on-chain data confirms that this wallet has completed its exit. It does not, by itself, establish the investor’s identity or explain the reason behind the decision to sell.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: Whale Selling Near $60K Adds to Glassnode’s Warning for Wall Street
summary: Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Thursday as whale distribution and weak demand added pressure to a market already struggling to regain its footing.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin traded near $60,000 on Thursday as whale distribution and weak demand added pressure to a market already struggling to regain its footing.

BTC recovered toward $60,400 on November 26 after falling to approximately $57,900 a day earlier. However, recent on-chain data suggests that selling pressure among large holders remains a concern for the market.

Santiment’s latest figures show that wallets holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC have reduced their combined balances by approximately 150,000 coins since November 2. Meanwhile, Glassnode warns that Bitcoin’s weakness could signal broader risk aversion across traditional financial markets.

Bitcoin Whales Reduce Holdings by 150K BTC

Santiment data shows that addresses holding between 10 and 10,000 BTC reduced their combined balances by around 150,000 BTC, representing a 1.1% decline since November 2. Their holdings fell from approximately 13.73 million BTC to 13.58 million BTC.

Bitcoin holdings have declined from their November 2 peak of 13.73 million BTC, suggesting continued selling pressure could prolong correction risks until accumulation resumes. Source: Santiment Intelligence via X

The distribution occurred as Bitcoin’s price declined 24.5%, falling from approximately $76,700 to $57,900 over the same period. Despite the reduction, this wallet cohort still controls around 67.55% of Bitcoin’s total circulating supply, making its accumulation and distribution patterns important indicators of market sentiment.

The data points to weakening conviction among a substantial group of Bitcoin holders. Continued balance reductions could increase the amount of available supply in the market, particularly when demand from new buyers remains limited.

However, changes in wallet balances do not establish the destination of every transferred coin or confirm that every movement represents an outright sale. The figures are best viewed as evidence of distribution within a defined wallet-size cohort.

A sustained reversal in this trend could provide a different signal. Stabilizing balances followed by renewed accumulation would suggest that these holders are becoming more comfortable with Bitcoin’s price levels.

Glassnode Sees Bitcoin Flashing a Warning for Wall Street

Glassnode’s latest market assessment highlights Bitcoin’s relative weakness following news that NVIDIA reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO, less than two weeks after his resignation.

The announcement initially triggered a rally across financial markets. Bitcoin gained approximately 5% in around 30 minutes alongside equities. However, the move quickly faded, with BTC giving back its entire advance in less than six hours. The Nasdaq 100, meanwhile, retained roughly three-quarters of its initial gain during that period.

Bitcoin led the market decline with a 5.5% drop, followed by the Nasdaq at 3.1% and the S&P 500 at 1.3%, while NVIDIA briefly rallied before retreating. Source: Glassnode via X

Glassnode described Bitcoin as the “canary in the coal mine,” arguing that its continuous trading makes it one of the first assets to reflect changing investor risk appetite. The research firm noted that stocks reacted more slowly but subsequently came under pressure as most of the Nasdaq’s initial gains disappeared.

The relationship between Bitcoin and traditional equities has also strengthened. According to Glassnode, the correlation between BTC and the Nasdaq 100 reached its highest level since September 2022, during the previous bear market.

This relationship matters because Bitcoin’s recovery could become more difficult if equity markets continue weakening. Glassnode also found that BTC has recently underperformed the Nasdaq on both positive and negative trading sessions, rising less when equities advance and falling more during declines.

Institutional demand presents another concern. Glassnode reported that US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $4.3 billion in net outflows over 20 trading days. Coinbase spot trading also showed persistent net selling among market takers over the previous 30 days.

These figures suggest that the US institutional buying interest that supported Bitcoin during its previous advance has weakened. A return of ETF inflows and stronger spot buying could provide evidence that demand is recovering.

$16B in Short Liquidations Could Fuel a Bitcoin Rebound

Despite the pressure from whale distribution and institutional outflows, Bitcoin’s derivatives market presents a potentially different picture.

CryptoQuant CEO Ki Young Ju highlighted an imbalance between potential short and long liquidations. According to his November 26 assessment, approximately $16 billion in short positions could face liquidation as BTC moves through the $60,000-$100,000 range. Potential long liquidations below $60,000, meanwhile, total less than $5 billion.

The chart highlights concentrated short liquidation exposure above $60,000, while long liquidation exposure at lower price levels remains limited. Source: Ki Young Ju via X

Ju stated that “The squeeze risk is on the short side,” pointing to the growing concentration of bearish leveraged positions.

A short squeeze occurs when rising prices force traders betting against an asset to close their positions. These traders may need to buy back Bitcoin to cover their exposure, potentially adding further upward pressure to the price.

The estimated liquidation imbalance could therefore create conditions for an accelerated recovery if Bitcoin attracts sufficient buying interest. However, the figures represent potential exposure rather than guaranteed liquidations. Price must reach the relevant liquidation levels before those positions are forced to close.

This distinction is important given the broader market environment. A concentration of short positions alone cannot reverse persistent spot selling or compensate for weakening demand. Bitcoin would still need sustained buying activity to establish a stronger upward trend.

Bitcoin’s 411-Day Decline Raises Questions About the Four-Year Cycle

Bitcoin’s longer-term performance also raises questions about whether its historical market cycle pattern will continue.

A recent CryptoQuant analysis compared the current downturn with previous Bitcoin cycles. The period from October 6, 2025, to November 21, 2026, spans 411 days, broadly matching the duration of several historical one-year declines.

Historical cycles show varying correction depths, with the 2026 downturn appearing severe, but past patterns alone do not confirm a market bottom without renewed demand. Source: CryptoQuant via X

The comparison has renewed attention on the familiar market pattern often described as “one year down, three years up.” Previous cycles showed lengthy recovery phases following deep corrections, but their timing does not establish a reliable schedule for future price movements.

The current drawdown also requires additional confirmation before it can be considered complete. CryptoQuant’s apparent demand indicators show both the 30-day and one-year metrics remaining below zero, suggesting that underlying demand has not recovered sufficiently.

Apparent demand estimates the relationship between new Bitcoin issuance and changes in the supply of coins that have remained inactive for more than a year. It provides insight into demand conditions but does not directly measure total spot purchases or net investment flows.

CryptoQuant’s analysis identifies a sustained improvement in this metric as an important condition for recovery. Stronger spot buying and renewed Bitcoin ETF inflows would also help demonstrate that buyers are absorbing available supply.

The analysis cautions against treating historical similarities as confirmation of a market bottom. As the contributor noted, “A durable recovery requires buyers willing to absorb supply.”

Bitcoin (BTC) Price Analysis

Bitcoin’s position around $60,000 remains an important test following its recent decline. Glassnode previously identified the $62,000-$66,000 region as a support area. However, BTC closed below this range on November 19, turning the previous support zone into potential resistance.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The cryptocurrency subsequently fell to approximately $55,300 on November 21 before recovering toward $60,000. Glassnode identified $58,500, corresponding to the June low, as another important level to monitor.

A convincing daily close below $60,000, followed by a break beneath $58,500, could expose Bitcoin to further downside. Glassnode placed its realized price—the average price at which coins last moved on-chain—near $53,200 as a potential lower reference level. This remains a conditional scenario rather than a confirmed price target.

On the upside, reclaiming the $62,000-$66,000 region would help improve Bitcoin’s immediate market structure. However, sustained recovery would require more than a short squeeze. Reduced whale distribution, stronger spot demand, and improving ETF flows would provide more meaningful evidence of a developing trend reversal.

For now, Bitcoin faces competing signals. The derivatives market shows considerable potential short-liquidation exposure, while on-chain distribution and weakening institutional demand continue to challenge recovery prospects. Whether BTC can stabilize near $60,000 may depend on whether fresh buyers emerge to absorb the available supply.

title: PEPE Whales Are Sitting On $21 Million In Tokens, And One Wallet Keeps Getting Bigger
summary: Key takeaways Lookonchain reports PEPE whales hold more than six trillion tokens, about $21.16 million, most of it in one wallet (0x5011) that has been buying since November 17. That wallet holds 5.15 trillion PEPE, roughly $18.28 million and about 1.22% of total supply; a second wallet (0x6246) hol...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Lookonchain reports PEPE whales hold more than six trillion tokens, about $21.16 million, most of it in one wallet (0x5011) that has been buying since November 17.
  • That wallet holds 5.15 trillion PEPE, roughly $18.28 million and about 1.22% of total supply; a second wallet (0x6246) holds 868.16 billion PEPE, about $2.88 million.
  • Not all large holders agree: Deep Blue Alpha data shows withdrawals were only about 36% of tracked whale transfers over seven days, so exchange deposits outweighed them.
  • Exchange deposits are not necessarily sales, and withdrawals do not prove a fresh purchase.
  • At this size, exiting at the quoted price depends on liquidity; a $0.000001 price move changes a 5.15 trillion position by $5.15 million.

PEPE whales have accumulated more than six trillion tokens worth approximately $21.16 million, according to new data from blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain. Most of that position belongs to a single unidentified wallet that has been accumulating the memecoin since November 17.

The size of the position is unusual even by memecoin standards. One address now holds more than 1% of PEPE’s entire supply, and its owner has continued adding tokens despite weakness in the market.

A Mystery PEPE Whale Keeps Adding To Its Position

The wallet, identified by its opening characters 0x5011, accumulated 5.15 trillion PEPE over eight days. Lookonchain valued the holdings at $18.28 million, representing approximately 1.22% of the cryptocurrency’s total supply.

The more interesting detail is how quickly the position has grown.

Lookonchain’s transaction monitoring history shows that by November 19, the wallet had withdrawn around 1.9 trillion PEPE from Binance. That figure climbed to 2.878 trillion by November 23 and exceeded 3.3 trillion the following day.

On Wednesday, Lookonchain reported that the address had accumulated 4.16 trillion tokens. By Thursday, its reported holdings had reached 5.15 trillion.

Another wallet, beginning with 0x6246, accumulated 868.16 billion PEPE valued at approximately $2.88 million, bringing the combined reported value to more than $21 million.

Large withdrawals are nothing new for the memecoin. NewsBTC previously covered a separate PEPE whale moving $14.7 million out of Binance. What makes the latest activity particularly interesting is the repeated accumulation within such a short period.

The Other Side Of The PEPE Whale Trade

Before treating these transactions as a bullish signal, it’s worth looking at what other large holders have been doing.

Data from blockchain analytics platform Deep Blue Alpha showed that withdrawals accounted for approximately 36% of tracked PEPE whale transfers between wallets and exchanges over the preceding seven days, according to its November 26 update.

In other words, exchange deposits outweighed withdrawals within that particular group of wallets.

That doesn’t invalidate Lookonchain’s findings. It does, however, complicate the idea that large investors are collectively preparing for a PEPE recovery.

One group of holders may be increasing its exposure while others are looking to reduce theirs. The distinction matters, especially in a market where a handful of transactions can attract more attention than the activity of dozens of other wallets.

Exchange deposits aren’t necessarily sales, just as withdrawals don’t establish that a fresh purchase has taken place. Centralized exchange trading records remain largely invisible to outside observers.

What A Trillion-Token Position Means For PEPE

For an investor holding 5.15 trillion PEPE, even a movement of $0.000001 in the token’s price would change the value of the position by $5.15 million.

That illustrates both the attraction and the risk of holding such a large quantity of a speculative asset.

Building an $18 million position is one thing. Exiting it at the quoted market price is another. The amount an investor can actually realize depends on available liquidity, execution and the market’s ability to absorb the tokens.

Concentrated holdings can therefore work in both directions. If tokens remain outside exchanges, they may reduce the supply immediately available for trading. If the same tokens return to exchanges, traders may suddenly find themselves watching for potential selling pressure.

The next development worth following is whether these wallets continue accumulating or begin transferring tokens back to trading platforms.

For now, two addresses hold an unusually large amount of PEPE. Whether the rest of the market shares their apparent appetite for the memecoin is a different question.

title: Crypto Market Maker Auros to Wind Down After Handling 4% of Global Exchange Trading
summary:
Key Takeaways: Auros, a Hong Kong-based crypto trading firm, is reportedly shutting down, CoinDesk reports based on two sources. The company once announced its volume scaling around 4% of all
The post Crypto Market Maker Auros to Wind Down After Handling 4% of Global Exchange Trading appeared first ...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Auros, a Hong Kong-based crypto trading firm, is reportedly shutting down, CoinDesk reports based on two sources.
  • The company once announced its volume scaling around 4% of all crypto exchange trades worldwide.
  • The FTX collapse saw Auross raise $17 million thereafter expanding into venture investments and institutional trading services.

Auros, a Hong Kong-based trading and market-making firm for cryptocurrencies, is also aiming at termination of operations. The reasons for the business closure and the timeline of the events have not been shared yet.

  • Auros Faces an Uncertain Exit from Crypto Markets
    • Potential Liquidity Impact on Crypto Exchanges
  • From FTX Restructuring to a $17 Million Fundraise
    • Auros Expanded into Venture Capital and Institutional Trading

Auros Faces an Uncertain Exit from Crypto Markets

According to a November 26 report by CoinDesk, two people familiar with the situation confirmed that Auros is winding down its operations. 

Auros, an established player in cryptocurrency markets since 2019, has been operating via algorithmic trading and market-making activities. In July 2024, CoinDesk reported that co-founder and Chief Investment Officer Ben Roth estimated that the firm services around 4% of all cryptocurrency exchange trading in the world.

Its own website also reported over $1.3 trillion in trading volume for 2025 with the highest average daily trading volume of $18.2 billion. These are estimates based on the firm’s reported trade and not independently verified market share.

Read More: Zapper Shuts Down After 7 Years, Ending a Journey That Processed $13B

Potential Liquidity Impact on Crypto Exchanges

The market maker ensures that the crypto market operates smoothly by keeping a balance between buyers and sellers. They actively improve order book liquidity and spreads on trading venues.

Auros’ exit may thus impact liquidity in the markets it is currently established. How much disruption it creates will depend on other firms filling in the trading space, and on how rapidly those other firms can do so.

From FTX Restructuring to a $17 Million Fundraise

Previously, Auros had been subjected to severe financial difficulties after the collapse of FTX, in November 2022. Its assets got stuck in the exchange, and it’s now in a court-supervised restructuring process in the British Virgin Islands.

In spite of the setback the matters were carried on as a going concern and negotiations were made with creditors. It raised $17 million during a round in March 2023, led by Vivienne Court, a trading firm, and backed by Bitcoin miner Bit Digital and others.

This currency, along with the debt structuring agreements, enabled Auros to emerge from provisional liquidation that same month.

Auros Expanded into Venture Capital and Institutional Trading

In later years the firm expanded its operations to run outside the bounds of market making. Auros made a pledge for its investment arm to invest over $50 million in early-stage crypto businesses over the next two years in July 2024. It invested in a variety of blockchain data providers, including Pyth, and network Berachain.

More recently, on September 29th, 2026, Auros introduced the Aurora institutional trading platform, which provides a unified access point to centralized exchanges as well as decentralized crypto markets.

The launch showed that Auros was still developing its institutional trading services shortly before news of its planned wind-down emerged.
