title: Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally
Bitcoin isn't a shiny new technology any more, it is established, and it is here to stay. 
This post Bitcoin Has Become Boring, Finally first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Roy Sheinfeld.
content:
The 2019 Lightning conference in Berlin was lit: five hundred “cypherpunks” getting each other high on visions of a future with peer-to-peer electronic cash. Attending a bitcoin conference back in the day felt like being a teenager at a friend’s party while their parents were out of town. It was exciting and new. The feeling was the opposite of FOMO: something big was happening, we were on the inside, and the rest of the world was going to envy us. It was the kind of party that you could only have when the adults weren’t looking. Whenever someone bought a beer (with bitcoin), everyone would hoot and holler and record it on their phones for Instagram/Twitter (it was still called Twitter).

Lightning was the bleeding edge. We called it “the Lightning Network” (capitalized, if you please), and talking about it felt like talking about string theory: something so far out you’re not even sure it’s real. I spent a lot of time invoking the abacus.

Those are the times some of us remember fondly and keep trying to relive at bitcoin conferences today. That’s why we engage in rituals like drone shows, Satoshi Rockamoto sets, beefsteak dinners, and video game tournaments for sats, but it’s not the same. The ratio of bitcoin OG speakers to suits is shifting. Many event rooms are half empty, and the halls and meeting rooms are full of people negotiating cap tables and profit-sharing splits.

The adults haven’t shut the party down, but they have crashed it, and it kinda feels like their party now. The most exciting thing I noticed at the last bitcoin conference I attended was that nothing exciting happened. 

And that’s worth celebrating.

From Tech Subcultures to Mainstream Tech Adoption

The road to boring is seldom smooth. Technological innovation benefits from passion and bold ideas. People work harder on a project when they feel strongly about it and identify closely with like-minded collaborators. That’s where tech subcultures, their rituals, and their dogmas come from. But such passion and tribalism feed conflict, at least for a while until the tech goes mainstream, and normies, who couldn’t care less about subculture squabbles, take over.

This progression from an exciting new technology that inspires strong emotions to a humdrum utility is not unusual. World-changing innovations often (always?) start with a committed subculture that identifies fiercely with their weird tech before the mainstream adopts it and soon expects it. In fact, this trajectory has become the standard doctrine of tech marketing. For example, in the early days of the internet, early adopters wrote a Declaration of the Independence of Cyberspace, picking a fight with states and corporations despite having nothing to back it up but chatrooms and dreams. 

One case that resembles the early days of bitcoin was the war of the currents between high-voltage AC current and low-voltage DC current in the 1880s-1890s. Both featured big personalities stunning audiences with flashy demos at conferences. Edison and Westinghouse wowed crowds with their lightbulbs that made artificial light, just like bitcoiners in 2019 wowed YouTube by buying beer with bitcoin. And both cases featured rabid subcultures that accused each other of putting the future of the technology, if not of humanity, at stake. In the 1880s, the issue was whether AC was more deadly to humans and animals than DC; in the 2010s it was whether limiting the size of bitcoin’s blocks to 1MB would perpetuate monetary servitude forever.

In both cases, there were devoted subcultures whose disagreements helped the technology to mature before the tech crossed the chasm of exoticism to become the new, boring normal. Both are now largely managed by experts on pragmatic principles, not passionate conviction. Conferences went from spectacular showcases for technological miracles to sedate affairs where professionals debate and agree on industry standards. Pragmatism and consensus replaced ideology and dissent. In both instances things got boring, and boring was actually better.

Mainstream Adoption Is Boring

Bitcoin is getting boring, although what that means and how it’s come to be that way depends on your point of view. As always, where you stand depends on where you sit. 

Generally speaking, there are two broad points of view on what bitcoin is and is for. And though they started in different places, they’re both coming to a common conclusion: bitcoin <yawn> is more boring than ever. So let’s review these two points of view, how they view bitcoin now, and why both would agree that the status quo is now so awfully, wonderfully boring.

The State of Bitcoin as a Tradable Asset

The basic existential question that defined bitcoin’s first decade is settled: bitcoin is not a scam, and it’s not going away. That status is stable largely because bitcoin is now too big to fail, with a market cap exceeding a trillion dollars. 

Much of this scale is thanks to the millions of people who want to own bitcoin as part of their savings, but not necessarily to trade and circulate it. In other words, they see bitcoin as a better form of gold, not cash. These savers want to integrate bitcoin into their fiat portfolio, just like any other asset. They aren’t terribly concerned about bitcoin’s status as a medium of exchange so long as it becomes firmly established as a viable, tradable commodity. 

People investing in bitcoin are happy when the number goes up, and it generally does (you might have to zoom out on the price graph a bit, depending on the week). Bitcoin used to be a rollercoaster; now it’s more of a hike. The ups and downs still happen, but they’re gentler and a bit more predictable. How boring.

Bitcoin’s price started to settle down as mainstream finance started growing more comfortable with it as an asset. Whereas conventional finance used to want governments to shut bitcoin down, there is now about $100B worth of bitcoin held in ETFs and traded on ordinary equity markets. Major banks used to shun bitcoin, and now they accept it as collateral. Bitcoin is a regular feature in corporate treasuries, and some companies exist just to hold bitcoin. Strategy is worth about $55B on the open market, and it holds about $63B worth of bitcoin, so the entire company is a discounted bitcoin wallet. Bitcoin is also a regular feature in retirement accounts, pension allocations, and sovereign wealth funds. Thinking of bitcoin as another kind of asset ripe for institutional and retail investors now makes a lot of sense, because that’s what it is.

Why are these canny investors bored? It seems that all the exciting developments leading to bitcoin becoming a valuable asset have already happened. If the goal was integration into the world of conventional finance, it has incontrovertibly been achieved. You can’t YOLO on bitcoin any more than you can YOLO on gold. The milestones are all in the history section of the Wikipedia page, not on the roadmap.

People who wanted bitcoin to become a tradable asset are bored because mainstream finance has effectively tamed bitcoin. It is easily tradable, and its trading volumes are remarkable. It is digital gold, just with a slightly steeper curve and a little more volatility, which is exactly what these folks always wanted.

The State of Bitcoin as P2P Electronic Cash

The main alternative to seeing bitcoin as a mainstream investment asset is to view it as monetary dynamite to ignite a revolution. People subscribing to this point of view wanted bitcoin to blossom into a system of peer-to-peer electronic cash that would first operate in parallel to the mainstream monetary system before supplanting it. These radicals wanted to see the banks collapse, not accept bitcoin as collateral. It was monetary insurrection, not incremental change.

This radical point of view is still around, but the wind has gone out of its combative sails for a few reasons. 

First, there has been a generational shift. Many of the people who were pushing the revolutionary vision of bitcoin in their 20s fifteen years ago have moved on. Some got rich and retired or started to see and use bitcoin more as a tradable asset. For others, bitcoin never achieved the success they dreamt of, but it was successful enough that fighting for its future no longer felt necessary.

Second, AI is the new cool kid on the tech block. Instead of building vending machines for beer that accept bitcoin, enthusiasts who want to hack the system are now decompiling games with AI. No VC will waste a second on a pitch deck that doesn’t have AI on at least half of the slides. Miners are turning their server stacks and power contracts into AI data centers. Curious engineers have a new, much bigger toy to play with.

Third, mainstream bitcoin fans on Wall Street simply consume too much bandwidth. Not surprisingly, banks, publicly traded companies, and financial institutions with billions in their pockets are dominating panels at conferences and supplying the talking heads for financial news shows. They want to discuss topics like volatility and discount rates instead of personal sovereignty and individual financial freedom. Fighting against the system is not a narrative they can sell while representing the interests of that very system. 

Fourth, bitcoin usage has moved past the radical mantras and progressed in a different direction. The dream of bitcoin becoming the standard payment medium in a circular economy where everyone buys coffee with bitcoin (why is it always coffee?) is starting to feel like an alternative history in a parallel universe. 

A circular economy is simply not the role in society bitcoin has grown into. Instead of everyday payments, bitcoin is the medium of global value transfer. It has evolved into a technology to move real money across borders as remittances, into a settlement layer between various crypto assets, and into a store of value that people constantly buy, sell, and trade. It’s become a valuable network of rails that even stablecoins are happy to use. 

Fixating on coffee purchases obscures the remarkable scale bitcoin has achieved. Somewhere between $1.6 and $4.1 trillion was settled on-chain between Q1 and Q3 2026 (depending on how you count). PayPal processed $1.79 trillion in all of 2025. The average payment on PayPal is about $70. The average bitcoin transaction (using the strict counting method) is $10,000. With bitcoin moving trillions in value, we can stop worrying about coffee.

Sources: Bitcoin, Mastercard, PayPal

Bitcoin may not have cornered retail payments, but it’s a mature and highly liquid asset. It’s an industry unto itself. It has found its place in the economy, and it’s thriving. Despite the lack of revolutionary fireworks, bitcoin is changing mainstream finance by opening new possibilities and financially enfranchising new user groups. That’s still worth celebrating. 

Awesome Reality > Perfect Fantasy

You know what’s really boring? Electricity infrastructure. You know what no one can live without despite how boring it is? Electricity infrastructure.

When revolutionary technologies fade into the background of everyday life, when people use them constantly without thinking about them, they become boring, and they become essential. Buying a beer with Lightning is no longer exciting because we can now expect that it will just work without fanfare. Being able to say “it will just work” sounds boring, but it’s a clear sign of triumph.

Bitcoiners and builders need to adjust to this beautiful, boring reality. We can stop annoying our neighbors with orange pills. It’s about utility, not evangelism. Utility means building rails that bitcoin and stablecoins can use together seamlessly, adding bitcoin to mainstream fintech apps, and building new financial applications on top of the bitcoin chain. Perhaps none of this will light the fireworks at the radicals’ victory party or replace T-bills as the base layer of global finance, but every user who discovers the unique utility of bitcoin is further evidence of its mainstream adoption.

What we have is a thriving technology that enables us to do miraculous new things, and it’s achieved an undeniable scale, such that it is now too big to fail. That’s fantastic. It may not be the future we were dreaming about seven years ago in Berlin, but it’s wonderful in its own right, and it’s worth cultivating and celebrating.

Even though nobody sets out to grow up and become boring one day, it’s still a valid kind of success. It means you’ve made it, and you’re doing fine. Boring is what happens when things just work and things have just worked out. So we didn’t break the world with bitcoin. Oh well. We’re making a new one. A party with adults present is still a party. And maybe we’re now the adults. So dance while you wait for the dollar to collapse 😉

MetaMask Card Expands to Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, Bringing Crypto to Mastercard
summary:
Key Takeaways: Metamask Card has been released in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam. Users can use crypto directly from self-custodial wallets at merchants using Mastercard. MetaMask says it is the card
The post MetaMask Card Expands to Japan, Thailand and Vietnam, Bringing Crypto to Mastercard appeared f...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Metamask Card has been released in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam.
  • Users can use crypto directly from self-custodial wallets at merchants using Mastercard.
  • MetaMask says it is the card issuer, as is Immersve Limited.

MetaMask has expanded its crypto payment card to 3 more Asian countries, providing options to spend digital assets with every transaction in Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam. The launch is the partnership of its self-custodial wallet service with Mastercard’s payment network.

  • MetaMask Brings Crypto Card to Three Asian Markets
  • Self-Custodial Wallets Meet Mastercard Payments
    • Spending Crypto Without Giving Up Wallet Control
    • MetaMask Pushes Further into Everyday Crypto Payments

MetaMask Brings Crypto Card to Three Asian Markets

MetaMask announced the expansion on November 25 through its official X account. MetaMask Card is now available to users in Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam where they can use it anywhere Mastercard is accepted, the company said.

MetaMask Card is now available in Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam.

Spend your crypto anywhere Mastercard is accepted, straight from your self-custodial wallet. ⤵️ https://t.co/nuhCNcCY7l

— MetaMask 🦊 (@MetaMask) November 25, 2026

The launch positions the wallet provider as increasingly popular in Asia, offering the user the ability to use a card-based payment method without the need to store money on a separate centralized exchange.

In announcing this change, MetaMask cited Immersve Limited as their card issuer. The company did not release any additional information regarding the business terms of the expansion or if all card features will be the same in the three countries.

It also failed to identify the conditions for launch, limits of spending or the complete list of supported cryptocurrencies in each market.

Read More: SBI Solana Global Goes Live, Bringing $2.3T Financial Giants into Onchain Finance

Self-Custodial Wallets Meet Mastercard Payments

One of the main aspects of MetaMask Card is its link with a self-custodial wallet. Self-custody is a different approach to a service, where the user doesn’t let go of the wallet or their own private keys from the apps.

Providing them with a new way to get everyday payments without relinquishing control over digital assets. In addition to investing and moving funds between wallets, crypto can also be used to make payments to participating merchants with supported assets.

Spending Crypto Without Giving Up Wallet Control

The Mastercard connection gives access to a constituted of merchants itself accepting the payment network. This means that no retailer will have to implement a third-party crypto payment service for the user to be able to utilize the card.

Acceptance of Mastercard doesn’t imply that all crypto and tokens in a particular individual’s MetaMask wallet can easily fund a purchase, though. Supported assets, terms of payment and conversion options vary by country.

MetaMask hasn’t given details on these figures in its launch post in Japan, Thailand and Vietnam.

MetaMask Pushes Further into Everyday Crypto Payments

The expansion introduces an additional payment use case to the wallet ecosystem of MetaMask. Self-custodial wallets have until now primarily been used to deposit tokens, interact with DApp and manage onchain assets.

Payment card is a more traditional means to transact outside the blockchain contexts. MetaMask is connecting wallet funds with an existing card network, launching an initiative to bring crypto transactions to a larger number of merchants.

The addition of Japan, Thailand, and Vietnam also extends the product’s reach across three distinct Asian markets. Whether the service gains wider adoption will depend on local availability, supported assets, fees, and the experience users receive when making payments.

One point matters more than any headline figure. Most of these platforms operate under offshore licenses such as Anjouan or Curaçao, which carry limited consumer-protection obligations compared with regimes like the UK or Malta. Several also market themselves as non-GamStop, which means UK users give up access to the Gambling Commission and UK dispute channels. The sections below cover what each platform offers and where its main limitations sit.

Roobet is the best pick in this list of the best crypto gaming sites, positioned as a broad digital gaming hub rather than a single-purpose platform. Launched in 2019, it offers 7,384 games from 81 providers, alongside sports and esports markets. The platform supports major cryptocurrencies including BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC, SOL, BNB, XRP, TRX, LTC, and DOGE, while also offering web and mobile-web access.

Pros of Roobet

  • Large game library with more than 7,000 titles from dozens of established providers.
  • Broad crypto support makes deposits and account funding flexible for digital-asset users.
  • Combines gaming, sports, esports, proprietary Roobet titles, and loyalty rewards within one account.

Cons of Roobet

  • The platform is unavailable in a number of restricted jurisdictions, including the United States and United Kingdom.
  • Mobile access is browser-based, with no dedicated app listed in the provided platform data.
  • The supplied information does not identify NFT ownership, staking, or marketplace functionality as core platform features.

Best Features of Roobet

  1. 7,384-Game Library: Roobet brings together slots, live gaming, table-style titles, and proprietary Roobet Games from 81 providers.
  2. Multi-Crypto Access: Users can fund accounts with major assets such as BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC, SOL, BNB, and DOGE.
  3. Roobet Rewards: Daily, weekly, and monthly rewards can include cashback, rakeback, RooSpins, and other account bonuses. roobet data

2. WSM

WSM is a Wall Street–themed platform offering live-dealer games and branded in-house titles, with a native token, $WSM, used for platform perks. It also accepts BTC, ETH, and $WSM to play on sports and esports markets.

Pros of WSM

  • Large game library covering predicting and sportsbook categories.
  • Native token gives access to staking and platform rewards.
  • Reload and match promotions available, subject to conditions.

Cons of WSM

  • Users report slow payout times, and support is not available around the clock.
  • Withdrawals above a set threshold require identity verification, and payouts are crypto-only.
  • Loyalty tiers are built around high wagering volumes, offering little to casual users.

Best Features of WSM

  1. VIP/Loyalty Program: A tiered system that unlocks cashback, faster withdrawals, and account-manager access as wagering volume rises. The tiers are set high, so the benefits apply mainly to frequent, high-volume users rather than casual ones.
  2. Welcome Promotion: A first-deposit match with a stated minimum deposit and playthrough conditions that determine how much credit becomes withdrawable.
  3. $WSM Token: A native token that can be staked for platform perks. As a crypto asset, its value fluctuates and staking carries the usual lock-up and market risk.

3. Instaspin

Instaspin is a modern NFT platform with unique social gaming features. Instaspin offers slots, table games, and live-dealer titles from established providers, with a social feature that lets users view and copy other players’ activity in real time.

Pros of Instaspin

  • Clean, easy-to-navigate interface with games grouped by category.
  • Broad selection of slots, table, and live-dealer games.
  • Offers a welcome package, though it carries playthrough requirements.

Cons of Instaspin

  • Access is restricted in certain countries.
  • Support is not 24/7, and some users report slow responses and concerns over promotional practices.
  • Operates outside GamStop, so self-excluded UK users lose UKGC recourse if a dispute arises.

Best Features of Instaspin

  1. Game Library: A categorized catalog of slots, table, and live-dealer titles from established providers.
  2. Non-GamStop Access: Available to UK users who have self-excluded from UKGC-licensed sites. This removes access to UK dispute and protection channels, so it is a limitation as much as a point of access.
  3. Live and Game-Show Titles: Live-dealer tables and game-show-style formats streamed from major providers, for users who prefer live over automated play.

4. Golden Panda

Golden Panda is an Asian-themed platform established in 2024 . The platform offers players 4,000+ games from top providers like Pragmatic Play, NetEnt, No Limit City, Evolution, and Hacksaw Gaming.

Pros of Golden Panda

  • Large game library from established providers, including a wide live-dealer section.
  • Offers 24/7 live chat and a match-based welcome promotion with defined conditions.
  • Includes a weekly cashback option without wagering on the cashback itself.

Cons of Golden Panda

  • Runs fewer ongoing promotions than comparable platforms.
  • Despite 24/7 chat, users report long queues and unresponsive email support.
  • Regional restrictions apply, so availability depends on location.

Best Features of Golden Panda

  1. Promotions: A match-based welcome offer with a stated minimum deposit, released in increments against a defined wagering requirement, plus a weekly cashback option.
  2. Live Streaming : A large live-dealer section with table games and game-show formats from established providers, including host interaction.

5. CoinPoker

CoinPoker is a crypto and NFT poker room that sponsors the Argentina football team. The NFT ecosystem mainly offers games in USDT. However, it allows traders to deposit and withdraw using other cryptocurrencies like BTC, ETH, and BNB. In addition to using USDT for games, it has its token, CHP, which is only used for bonuses.

Pros of CoinPoker

  • On-chain RNG lets users independently verify game fairness.
  • Covers a wide range of sports markets in addition to poker.
  • Offers a first-deposit promotion with a stated minimum and conditions.

Cons of CoinPoker

  • Focused on poker, with fewer general gaming categories than competitors.
  • Withdrawals are limited to private wallets, with no centralized-exchange support.
  • Requires a self-custody wallet, which adds a step for less experienced users.

Best Features of CoinPoker

  1. Mobile App: Native apps for iOS and Android, installed directly rather than through app stores.
  2. Tournaments: A regular schedule of buy-in tournaments and series with varying formats and prize pools. Entry requires a buy-in, and prize pools are shared among participants.
  3. Bad Beat Jackpot: A shared poker prize pool funded by table rake that pays out when a strong hand loses to a stronger one, distributed among players under set conditions.

6. Instant Casino

Instant Casino is an online NFT platform launched in 2024. The platform offers about 4,000 games, including slots, classic table games, live prediction games, and specialty games like Bingo and Scratch Cards. The games are powered by top providers such as Microgaming, NetEnt, Evolution, Pragmatic Play, and Red Tiger, providing high-quality graphics and gameplay. With the fast payout system, this business processes withdrawal requests instantly.

Pros of Instant Casino

  • Fast withdrawal processing compared with many peers.
  • Offers a welcome promotion and cashback, with cashback free of wagering.
  • Pay’n Play access in supported countries removes a registration step.

Cons of Instant Casino

  • Some users report delays with larger withdrawals despite the instant-payout claim.
  • Limited responsible-use tools compared with peers.
  • Not available in several major markets, including the US, UK, France, and Germany.

Best Features of Instant Casino

  1. Sports Partnership Promotions: Time-limited campaigns tied to a football-club partnership, offering experience-based and merchandise rewards through periodic draws.
  2. Provider Drop Campaigns: Participation in a provider-run promotion with periodic prize drops across selected slots and live games, subject to that provider’s terms.

7. Mega Dice

Mega Dice gained recognition as the first entertainment hub to operate via Telegram. It allows players to access games and play directly in the app via a Telegram bot. Mega Dice offers 5,000+ games, including slots, game shows, table games, live games, dice games, and sports predicting.

Pros of Mega Dice

  • Accessible through both a website and a Telegram interface.
  • Large game library from a wide range of providers.
  • Uses standard security measures, including SSL and two-factor authentication.

Cons of Mega Dice

  • Primarily crypto-based, with limited fiat options.
  • Promotions carry high playthrough conditions.
  • Token staking ties users to variable, non-guaranteed returns with lock-up periods, a risk separate from gameplay.

Best Features of Mega Dice

  1. Telegram Access: Core functions, including deposits, withdrawals, and gameplay, are available through a Telegram bot in addition to the website.
  2. Token Staking: The $DICE token can be locked in fixed-term pools for variable returns. Returns are not guaranteed, unstaking carries a withdrawal lock, and the token is exposed to market volatility, so this is a financial-risk feature rather than a reward.
  3. $DICE Token: A native utility token used for platform access, governance participation, and promotions.

8. Lucky Block

Lucky Block is a cryptocurrency-based online gaming platform launched in 2022. The platform offers a wide range of games, including 4,000 games alongside a sportsbook covering more than 35 sports markets. Aside from featuring games from top providers, it also offers provably fair games using blockchain technology to ensure fair play.

Lucky Block integrates its native LBLOCK token, providing users with perks such as rakebacks, cashback, tailored promotions, staking opportunities, and exclusive NFT-based VIP experiences.

Pros of Lucky Block

  • Provably fair games verifiable on-chain.
  • Large game library including live-dealer and poker options.
  • Offers instant deposits and quick withdrawals for most methods.

Cons of Lucky Block

  • Bonus terms are complex, with layered wagering that makes credit hard to convert to withdrawable funds.
  • Access is restricted in several countries, including the US, UK, Australia, and France.
  • Staking returns are variable and carry standard crypto-asset risk.

Best Features of Lucky Block

  1. VIP Club: A tier for frequent users offering cashback and rakeback that scale with activity, along with a dedicated manager at higher levels. The thresholds favor high-volume play.
  2. Loyalty Program: A tier-based system where users progress by meeting wagering thresholds regardless of outcome, unlocking cashback and free spins.
  3. $LBLOCK Staking: Native-token staking with returns that vary by amount and lock-up length. As with any crypto asset, returns are variable and principal is at market risk.

9. Wreckbet

WreckBet is a new, pirate-themed gaming platform offering a broad game selection and generous bonuses. It is licensed offshore under Curacao and Anjouan, but not regulated by the UK Gambling Commission (UKGC). Still, it primarily targets and offers services to UK players seeking non-GamStop options.

Pros of Wreckbet

  • 24/7 support, generally reported as responsive.
  • Broad game and sportsbook selection for a newer platform.
  • Offers a welcome promotion and weekly reloads, subject to conditions.

Cons of Wreckbet

  • Not regulated by the UK Gambling Commission; targets UK users through non-GamStop access, which removes UKGC recourse.
  • Promotions carry high playthrough conditions.
  • Loyalty structure favors high-volume users, offering little to casual ones.

Best Features of Wreckbet

  1. Sportsbook Promotions: A rewards layer on multi-leg places and a refund mechanism on certain tennis outcomes, both governed by specific qualifying conditions.
  2. Loyalty Program: A points-based system that unlocks cashback on losses and free spins as users progress. Milestones are set high, so casual users advance slowly, and it lacks the account-management perks found on some other platforms.

10. BC.Game

BC.Game is a leading Web3 entertainment and online gaming platform blending traditional games with blockchain technology to give users immersive gaming experiences. Established in 2017, the platform operates as a licensed crypto gaming hub and sportsbook, offering various online games, sports predicting, and lottery options.

Pros of BC.Game

  • Long operating history and a large game library, including in-house titles.
  • Active community features and regular platform updates.
  • Offers a welcome promotion and loyalty rewards with defined terms.

Cons of BC.Game

  • Crypto-only, with no fiat support, exposing users to asset volatility and removing chargeback protection.
  • Complex bonus terms with high playthrough conditions.
  • Some users report above-average withdrawal fees.

Best Features of BC.Game

  1. Community Forum: An official forum covering platform updates, game discussion, support, and token topics, with active user participation.
  2. VIP Club: A loyalty program that scales with activity, unlocking periodic bonuses, higher rakeback, and event access at higher tiers.
  3. NFT Promotions: Periodic campaigns distributing blockchain-based collectibles across supported chains, which users can hold, trade, or use in platform events.

What Are the NFT Gaming Sites?

NFT gaming sites are online predicting platforms that use non-fungible tokens as part of the gaming experience. Instead of relying solely on fiat currencies or even cryptocurrencies like some digital entertainment hubs, these sites integrate NFTs for deposits, wagering, rewards, ownership, or access to exclusive features.

While the use cases of NFTs in online entertainment are still unfolding, some sites allow players to wager with NFTs directly or use them to unlock special games, bonuses, or VIP experiences. In some cases, owning specific NFTs might give users a stake in the platform’s profits or access to community voting rights.

What are the Benefits of Playing at NFT Gaming Hub?

The benefits of playing at NFT gaming hub are provably fair gaming, faster and private transactions, exclusive rewards, and passive earning potential through staking. First, the platforms use blockchain technology to ensure game transparency and fairness. Every transaction and game outcome can be verified on the blockchain, enhancing trust between players and operators.

Secondly, players enjoy faster, more secure, and more private transactions since they can register with KYC verification at some gaming platforms. Aside from KYC, using cryptocurrencies and NFTs allows for quick, safe, and often anonymous transactions without traditional banking intermediaries, reducing costs and speeding up deposits and withdrawals.

Finally, playing at NFT gaming hub can be seen as an entertainment and investment opportunity. Some platforms like Roobet, Mega Dice, and Lucky Block allow players to stake their crypto holdings for a specific period, usually starting at 30 days, in exchange for profits.

What are the NFT Gaming Bonuses?

Promotional credit on these platforms usually takes the form of welcome offers, free spins, reload credit, and loyalty or VIP rewards. The important detail is not the advertised size of these offers but their conditions. Most come with playthrough (wagering) requirements that determine how much, if any, of the credit can eventually be withdrawn, and these conditions vary widely between platforms.

Referral credit is also common, where an existing user and a new user both receive rewards after the new user signs up and meets requirements. The mechanism resembles referral programs on mainstream exchanges; for a comparison on regulated trading platforms, this crypto sign-up bonus guide covers referral offers across major exchanges.

What are the Differences Between NFT Gaming Sites vs Traditional Play Hub?

The differences between NFT gaming sites vs traditional play hubs are anonymity and privacy, supported currencies, access, rewards, transaction speed, and security. While traditional online gaming hubs often require identity verification and personal details, NFT entertainment systems usually allow players to participate using just a crypto wallet, offering a more private experience.

Regarding supported currencies, NFT/crypto predicting sites rely on digital assets, whereas traditional entertainment platforms primarily operate with fiat currencies. In terms of access, NFT gaming sites are usually open to anyone with an internet connection and a crypto wallet, as long as the platform you choose is not restricted in your region.

Thanks to blockchain technology, transaction speed is faster on NFT gaming platforms, enabling near-instant deposits and withdrawals. In contrast, traditional gaming transactions can be slower due to banking processes.

Lastly, NFT entertained sites operate on decentralized systems, offering transparent smart contracts and provably fair games, while traditional sites rely on centralized systems that require trust in the house’s fairness.

How to Choose the Best NFT Gaming Sites to Play?

Before using any NFT-linked platform, assess it against factors that affect user protection more than promotional appeal: licensing and regulation, game structure, supported assets, promotional terms, security, user experience, and transaction costs.

  1. Licensing and Regulation: Verify that the NFT sites hold a reputable license (e.g., Curaçao, Malta) to ensure that they operate legally and follow regulatory standards for player protection.
  2. Game Variety: Look for platforms offering a wide range of games, including slots, live games, table games, and NFT-specific games. Top sites like Mega Dice and BC.Game offers thousands of titles from leading software providers, ensuring quality and diversity.
  3. Supported Cryptocurrencies and NFTs: Choose NFT sites that support multiple cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum, Dogecoin, USDC, etc.) and allow you to use, earn, or trade NFTs easily.
  4. Bonuses and Promotions: Evaluate welcome bonuses, free spins, reloads, cashback, and ongoing promotions. Some NFT hubs offer generous packages, but check the wagering requirements and fairness of terms.
  5. Security and Privacy: Ensure the site uses strong encryption and privacy measures. NFT sites often allow anonymous play with crypto wallets, reducing the need for personal data submission. The best NFT platforms should have secure NFT wallet integration like MetaMask, Coinbase, Binance, or eToro.
  6. User Experience: A smooth, intuitive interface enhances gameplay. Some sites may have cluttered layouts due to many offerings, so choose one that balances features with ease of use.
  7. Transaction Speed and Fees: Look for fast deposits and withdrawals with low fees. Crypto transactions offer instant processing compared to traditional fiat methods. If you are new to NFT gaming sites or the crypto space in general, read this guide on how to buy meme coins for a straightforward process to transfer crypto from one wallet to another.

How Do NFT Gaming Sites Work?

NFT gaming sites work by letting players use NFTs to fund their accounts and play game on classic prediction games, ranging from slots and table games to bingo and crypto-native titles. Instead of crypto or fiat currencies, these platforms use NFTs as a medium of exchange, offering a decentralized and secure gaming environment to play online. But beyond gameplay, some sites are exploring ways to provide NFTs as welcome bonuses, part of loyalty rewards, or even cashback.

title: MOEX Derivatives Revenue Surges 52% Outpacing CME and ICE
summary:
Derivatives generated RUB 4.63 billion ($56.2 million) in fee and commission income on MOEX during Q3, up nearly 53% year on year. Growth was registered across currency, index and commodity contracts, while the currency derivatives showed the best result, with turnover jumping 81%. 
Trading volume r...
content:
2026-11-26T16:40:58.157+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 14:40 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Currency and index derivatives drove quarterly turnover to $670.1 billion.
  • MOEX followed the global direction of rising derivatives activity, but its product mix was local.

Derivatives generated RUB 4.63 billion ($56.2 million) in fee and commission income on MOEX during Q3, up nearly 53% year on year. Growth was registered across currency, index and commodity contracts, while the currency derivatives showed the best result, with turnover jumping 81%.

Trading volume reached RUB 55.16 trillion ($670.1 billion), compared with RUB 33.96 trillion ($412.6 billionº in Q3 2025, an increase of 62.4%, according to the MOEX's report.

Derivatives market indicatorQ3 2026 change
Fee and commission income+52.4%
Total trading volume+62.4%
Currency derivatives volume+81.0%
Index derivatives volume+71.1%
Commodity derivatives volume+46.9%

The Exchange Added 37 Contracts during the Quarter

Fee income continued to grow more slowly than turnover. Moscow Exchange noted a shift in trading toward currency and index derivatives, with higher-value commodity contracts making up a smaller share of activity. This in turn reduced the effective fee earned per rouble of trading volume.

The exchange launched 37 derivatives contracts in the quarter, including perpetual futures on global assets and crypto indices as well as a futures contract on its key rate index.

After the reporting period, MOEX added another 29 futures, including 27 perpetual contracts linked to foreign equities. This brought its range of perpetual futures on global assets to 54 instruments.

MOEX Outpaces the Wider Derivatives Expansion

MOEX's results were in line with the wider trend of increased derivatives trading, though their growth rate was higher by a considerable margin. CME Group's ADV was up 16% year on year in Q3, ICE's was up 31% year on year.

MOEX's 62.4% increase is quite striking, though the two figures are not directly comparable. MOEX reports rouble turnover whereas the others are reporting contracts or average daily activity.

The underlying pattern also differed. As Finance Magnates previously reported, CME generated record quarterly revenue even though its ADV fell 1.3% from Q2.

Two additional trading days lifted the estimated total number of contracts, while revenue per contract hardly changed. MOEX on the other hand saw a significant year on year increase in turnover, driven by currency and index products.

Margex bonus can be claimed by all new users on the exchange. But remember, the platform is not available in the United States, Seychelles, Bermuda, Cuba, Iran, Syria, North Korea, Sudan, and other restricted areas. What are the requirements?

  • You genuinely just need to register an account to unlock the $50 sign-up bonus.
  • You must claim your bonus from the “Promo Code Storage”, since it doesn’t credit itself automatically.
  • Plus, deposit at least $100 within 7 days to claim the “First Deposit Bonus” as well.
  • You can treat your bonus funds as cashback, not free cash, since they cover up to 50% of trading fees and funding costs once trades close.

Verdict on the Margex Offer

The Margex offer has one of the easiest entry points because the $50 sign-up credit needs no large trading target. Mainly, its real value remains limited to fee and funding cost coverage. So, it works best for someone who already plans to use Margex leverage trading.

How We Verified These Welcome Bonus Offers?

We verified these welcome offers by checking the four criteria: offer value, trading volume requirement, expiration, and eligible regions.

  • Offer value: We separated the headline maximum from the amount a normal new user can reach. You see, a package worth 30,000 USDT may include a small sign-up reward, but a much larger futures tier for high-volume traders. We also checked whether the reward comes as withdrawable crypto, a fee rebate, a mystery box, a trading bonus, or a trial fund.
  • Trading Volume requirement: We compared the required net deposit with the spot or futures volume needed for each tier. Plus, we also checked common exclusions such as internal transfers, zero-fee trades, API activity, bot volume, and subaccounts.
  • Duration: We checked how long you have to finish a task, claim a completed reward, and use the claimed voucher. You see, every crypto exchange sign-up bonus has an expiry date, generally within 30 days of registration.
  • Eligible regions: We compared the campaign country rules with each exchange’s current restricted-location terms. A referral link may open in your browser even though your verified country cannot join the offer. We also treated U.S. versions of Binance and OKX as separate services because their global bonuses and products do not automatically carry over.

Are crypto sign-up bonuses worth it?

Yes, crypto sign-up bonuses are genuinely worth claiming in most cases, as long as you go in with realistic expectations about what you’ll actually receive. 

The instant, low-effort tiers, like Binance’s KYC voucher or even Margex’s flat $50, cost you basically nothing beyond a few minutes of setup. But again, the bigger headline numbers, like Bybit’s $30,020 or MEXC’s $10,000, require serious capital and trading volume that most casual users will never reach, so you should treat those as aspirational rather than expected.

You see, no-deposit bonus offers are rare, and a free crypto sign-up bonus with instant withdrawal usually comes with a lock, KYC step, or trading condition. The better way is to value a bonus at what you can personally use. Also, most of the bonus funds usually arrive as trading credit or vouchers rather than withdrawable cash. Hence, at least at first, read the terms before assuming you can cash out immediately.

Which crypto exchange sign-up bonus is the best for your trading type?

The best crypto sign-up bonus, or welcome reward, depends more on how you plan to use the exchange. According to the definition of crypto welcome bonus, the first-time account openers may benefit more from simple deposit or first-trade rewards, while buy-and-hold investors should look for those bonuses that never require heavy trading, and frequent traders often get more from fee discounts and similar exchange promotions.

Next, high-frequency and grid traders can usually get more value from trading-fee rebates, volume-based sign-up rewards, and futures bonuses because they trade more often.

First-Time Account Openers

First-time account openers should choose a bonus with very simple requirements and a low minimum deposit. You know, a reward for completing KYC, making your first deposit, or placing a few trades makes more sense than a large bonus that requires thousands of dollars in trading volume. Hence, you should mainly focus on how easy the reward is to unlock rather than its maximum advertised value.

Buy-and-Hold Investors

Buy-and-hold investors should look for deposit bonuses or rewards that require little trading. Basically, a $50 reward after depositing and buying crypto can be more useful than a $500 futures bonus that requires active trading. Plus, you should also avoid promotions that force you to generate high trading volume because frequent buying and selling does not match a long-term investment strategy.

High-Frequency and Grid Traders

High-frequency and grid traders can benefit most from bonuses linked to trading volume. Here, fee rebates, futures credits, trading vouchers, and volume-based rewards become more valuable because you naturally place many trades. Hence, a bonus with a higher trading requirement may therefore make sense for you, provided the normal trading fees and conditions remain competitive.

Are free crypto sign-up bonuses available for every exchange?

No, free crypto sign-up bonuses are not available on every exchange. Not every platform uses the same signup structure, and some reserve free bitcoin or similar promotions for app-based campaigns or limited regions. Basically, each platform decides its own promotion rules, and some exchanges do not offer any reward just for creating an account.

Even exchanges that advertise a welcome bonus usually ask you to complete certain steps first. So, you may need to verify your identity, deposit a minimum amount, make your first trade, or reach a required trading volume. The reward can also vary by country, campaign period, and referral link.

Can I withdraw my free crypto bonuses immediately?

No, you cannot withdraw a free crypto bonus immediately, as most exchanges place conditions on the reward because the bonus is meant to encourage real trading activity, not simply give away withdrawable cash.

You should also check the exchange app terms carefully, since bonuses can vary by region and some platforms use promotions to grow their user base.

You may need to deposit funds, complete KYC, make a certain number of trades, or reach a required trading volume before the bonus even becomes eligible for withdrawal. Plus, some rewards cannot be withdrawn at all. So, for example, futures bonuses and trading credits may only cover trading losses or fees, while you can withdraw the profits earned from them under certain rules.

Of course, this works differently from exchange to exchange. Hence, you should always check the withdrawal terms first, especially the minimum trading requirement, expiry date, and whether the bonus itself or only the profits can be withdrawn.

title: Zcash Whale Wakes Up After 9 Years, Moves $11.39 Million To Kraken
summary: Key takeaways Lookonchain reports a Zcash whale moved 15,750 ZEC, about $11.39 million, to Kraken after nine years. The whale reportedly bought 23,412 ZEC in 2017 at about $215 (just over $5 million). The deposit is roughly two-thirds of that position. At about $723 per ZEC, the coins are worth arou...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Lookonchain reports a Zcash whale moved 15,750 ZEC, about $11.39 million, to Kraken after nine years.
  • The whale reportedly bought 23,412 ZEC in 2017 at about $215 (just over $5 million). The deposit is roughly two-thirds of that position.
  • At about $723 per ZEC, the coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated cost, a gain of roughly 236%.
  • A deposit to an exchange is not proof of a sale, and the acquisition price is an estimate, not a verified record.
  • More early holders moving dormant coins to exchanges could mean new Zcash buyers absorb supply from older holders.

Nine years is an eternity in crypto. Yet one Zcash whale appears to have spent that long sitting on an investment made during the privacy coin’s early days. On Thursday, blockchain monitoring platform Lookonchain reported that the investor had moved 15,750 ZEC, worth $11.39 million, to Kraken.

The coins date back to 2017, when Ethereum was still a relatively young network, decentralized finance barely existed and Zcash was attempting to establish itself as a more private alternative to Bitcoin.

Almost a decade later, the wallet is active again. And its owner’s reported acquisition price makes the transaction particularly interesting.

A $5 Million Bet On Zcash In 2017

According to Lookonchain, the whale originally acquired 23,412 ZEC at an average price of approximately $215, representing an investment of just over $5 million.

The latest transactions account for roughly two-thirds of that original position, with at least 7,750 ZEC transferred to a Kraken deposit address.

At the reported transfer valuation of approximately $723 per ZEC, those 15,750 coins are worth around $8 million more than their estimated acquisition cost. That would represent a return of approximately 236% if the investor sold them at that price.

What makes this wallet fascinating, however, is what happened between those two valuations.

Zcash spent much of 2024 and early 2025 trading around $16 to $20 before staging a remarkable comeback. At $20 per coin, the whale’s original investment would have been worth less than $470,000, a paper loss of more than 90%, assuming the position remained intact.

Holding an asset through a temporary market correction is one thing. Holding it through years of declining relevance, while newer cryptocurrencies attract developers, investors and attention, is something else entirely.

Whatever the owner’s reasons for keeping the coins untouched, the decision has aged considerably better than it appeared to during Zcash’s quieter years.

The Interesting Paradox Behind A Zcash Whale

There is something almost ironic about the fact that investors are following the movements of a whale holding one of crypto’s best-known privacy coins.

Unlike networks where transaction privacy is mandatory, Zcash supports both transparent and shielded transactions. Transparent addresses allow observers to examine balances and transfers, while shielded transactions use zero-knowledge cryptography to conceal transaction details.

That distinction explains how blockchain monitoring platforms can identify certain large ZEC movements despite the cryptocurrency’s privacy capabilities.

It also explains why the available information tells only part of the story.

Lookonchain can identify an apparent exchange deposit and estimate its value. Establishing who controls the wallet, whether ownership changed privately during those nine years or what the investor intends to do next is considerably harder.

Even the reported acquisition price is an estimate rather than a verified record of the owner’s personal trading history.

That is an important limitation of on-chain analysis, particularly when dealing with a network explicitly designed to give users greater control over their financial visibility.

Zcash’s Comeback Has Given Early Investors An Exit

The renewed enthusiasm surrounding Zcash has attracted a different kind of investor from the one buying ZEC in 2017.

Corporate treasury strategies have emerged, institutional investors have taken an interest in privacy-focused assets, and the debate over financial surveillance has given Zcash a fresh investment narrative.

NewsBTC previously reported that Winklevoss Capital backed the launch of a dedicated Zcash treasury strategy, illustrating how exposure to the cryptocurrency has begun extending beyond traditional crypto wallets.

But the revival of an old cryptocurrency also comes with an interesting complication: investors who have spent years underwater finally have an opportunity to recover their capital or take profits.

That does not necessarily make the Kraken deposit bearish. A transfer to an exchange is not proof of a completed sale, and one wallet cannot establish a broader trend among Zcash holders.

Still, the transaction is worth watching. If more early investors start moving dormant coins onto exchanges, Zcash’s new buyers may find themselves absorbing supply from an entirely different generation of holders.

Nine years ago, someone reportedly committed more than $5 million to the idea of private digital money. Today, the blockchain offers a glimpse of what that investment has become.

Whether the owner has finished holding Zcash is a question the blockchain alone cannot yet answer.

summary:
MetaQuotes warned brokers of a surge in distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) and hacking attacks targeting their infrastructure, urging firms to overhaul server redundancy to prevent prolonged outages and data loss.
“We are aware of cases where attacks resulted not only in prolonged trading platform...
content:
2026-11-26T14:40:27.956+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 12:40 GMT by Adonis Adoni

  • While it didn’t disclose how many brokers were affected, the platform provider identified the main reason as inadequate infrastructure redundancy.
  • The warning follows major financial sector cyberattacks, including the Binance hack ($6.3 billion drained) and GMO Internet Group VPS breach affecting Japanese FX brokers.

MetaQuotes warned brokers of a surge in distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) and hacking attacks targeting their infrastructure, urging firms to overhaul server redundancy to prevent prolonged outages and data loss.

“We are aware of cases where attacks resulted not only in prolonged trading platform downtime (with corresponding financial losses), but also in partial loss of trading data (which is a very serious matter),” MetaQuotes said in an email sent Wednesday from its support center.

The platform provider identified the main reason as inadequate infrastructure redundancy, and has advised brokers to “conduct a thorough review of their trading infrastructure. If necessary, revise it.”

It advised brokers to maintain at least two backup servers for the trading server and history server to ensure comprehensive backups. That, it said, is the bare minimum. In practice, it recommends four or more backup servers, at least three access points per trading server and additional access points in each significant geographic area.

MetaQuotes didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

Hacking Attacks on the Rise

The platform provider’s advisory comes amid a wave of high-profile cyberattacks across financial markets that has pushed operational resilience to the top of corporate agendas.

On October 29, attackers drained roughly $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency from hot wallets at Binance across multiple blockchains in about 20 minutes, though stablecoin issuers subsequently froze nearly $3 billion of the funds.

A post-mortem from the exchange revealed a multi-month intrusion involving a tampered artificial-intelligence coding tool in June and a fake recruitment interview in September that compromised engineers’ devices, allowing attackers to move laterally to an internal wallet-signing service. The US Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed the heist to North Korea’s Lazarus Group, an allegation Pyongyang’s Kim Yo Jong denied.

In Japan, a cyberattack on GMO Internet Group Inc.’s Onamae.com Desktop Cloud, a virtual private server service frequently used by retail traders to run MetaTrader terminals, compromised up to 26,739 servers and exposed stored brokerage credentials.

GMO began shutting down servers sequentially on October 21 and later refused a $50 million ransom demand, after which attackers leaked customer data. Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said five foreign-exchange firms, including Goldenway Japan and Oanda Securities, were affected.

GMO set aside roughly 3 billion yen ($19.5 million) to compensate affected users.

Regulators have increasingly highlighted that attackers are targeting retail traders. In November, the IOSCO warned that self-directed, social-media-active retail investors are among the hardest-hit groups, citing account takeovers and fraudulent withdrawals executed via phishing, deepfakes, synthetic identities and cloned brokerage websites.

title: US Senators Warn SEC’s Crypto Proposal Could Weaken Securities Laws and Oversight
summary: U.S. senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen have urged the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to withdraw two crypto-related measures, warning they could weaken investor protections and create regulatory loopholes.
content:
Skip to content

U.S. senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen have urged the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to withdraw two crypto-related measures, warning they could weaken investor protections and create regulatory loopholes.

In letters sent to SEC Chair Paul Atkins on November 24, the lawmakers challenged the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework and a separate exemption for tokenized securities trading platforms. They argued that the measures could give crypto businesses preferential treatment while reducing safeguards that apply to traditional financial markets. The Senate Banking Committee publicized the requests on November 25.

Warren Challenges SEC’s Crypto Fundraising Proposal

Warren, joined by Van Hollen and Senator Tina Smith, called on the SEC to rescind Regulation Crypto Assets, which the agency introduced on August 18, 2026. The proposal seeks to establish a separate framework for certain investment contracts involving crypto assets, allowing eligible issuers to raise capital through exemptions from conventional securities registration requirements.

Senator Elizabeth Warren urged SEC Chair Paul Atkins to withdraw the proposed Regulation Crypto Assets rule, arguing it grants crypto firms excessive regulatory freedom. Source: @CoinMarketCap/X

The proposed framework includes two fundraising pathways. A one-time startup exemption would allow eligible crypto projects to raise up to $5 million over four years. A separate fundraising exemption would permit offerings of up to $75 million during any 12-month period. Both pathways would require principles-based disclosures, while the larger exemption would also require financial statements and ongoing reporting.

The proposal includes a conditional investment contract safe harbor. Under this provision, a crypto asset could cease to be treated as subject to an investment contract under federal securities laws once an issuer permanently ends the essential managerial efforts associated with the original agreement and satisfies other specified conditions.

Warren and her colleagues argue that these provisions create an easier route for crypto companies to avoid regulatory requirements faced by traditional securities issuers. In their letter, the senators said the framework gives digital assets “special treatment—with less oversight” compared with conventional securities.

They also questioned the level of scrutiny applied to projects using the proposed exemptions. According to the lawmakers, the startup exemption would not require financial statements or prior SEC approval, while its disclosure requirements would provide considerably less information than those associated with comparable traditional securities offerings.

Senators Raise Concerns Over Investor Protection and State Oversight

The senators outlined several concerns about the potential consequences of the proposed SEC crypto rules, particularly their implications for retail investors and state securities regulators.

One central issue involves the possibility of fraudulent fundraising. Warren argued that allowing crypto projects to raise substantial amounts without the usual registration and disclosure requirements could leave investors with limited information about issuers, their finances, and their business operations.

Senators Warren and Van Hollen urged SEC Chair Paul Atkins to rescind proposed crypto rules and exemptions for tokenized securities venues. Source: The Block via X

The letter also questioned the absence of certain safeguards commonly associated with other exempt securities offerings. These include requirements for independent intermediaries and restrictions on the resale of securities. The lawmakers argued that without such protections, insiders could potentially sell their holdings before investors fully understand the risks surrounding a project.

State-level enforcement represents another point of disagreement. The SEC proposal would preempt state securities registration and qualification requirements for offerings conducted under the new exemptions, along with certain related secondary-market transactions.

Warren argued that this provision could remove an additional layer of investor protection, particularly in situations where federal registration requirements no longer apply. The senators maintained that state regulators should retain authority to address questionable offerings and protect investors in their jurisdictions.

The lawmakers also challenged the SEC’s legal authority to establish the framework without further congressional action. Their letter argues that the proposal exceeds the agency’s statutory powers and conflicts with the legal principles governing the classification of investment contracts.

In particular, they questioned its treatment of the Howey Test, the Supreme Court standard established in the 1946 case SEC v. W.J. Howey Co. The test remains central to determining whether an arrangement qualifies as an investment contract and therefore falls within federal securities regulation.

Van Hollen Questions SEC’s Tokenized Securities Exemption

The senators’ objections extend beyond crypto fundraising. In a separate letter, led by Van Hollen and joined by Warren, Smith and Senator Jack Reed, lawmakers asked Atkins to withdraw an SEC order issued on September 17, 2026.

The order, known as the Innovation Exemption, grants temporary and conditional relief to certain Tokenized Securities Venues (TSVs) and liquidity providers. It allows qualifying distributed-ledger trading platforms to operate outside the statutory definition of an exchange, while certain liquidity providers receive exemptions from dealer registration requirements.

These platforms facilitate trading in tokenized versions of stocks listed on the national market system. The technology represents conventional securities through blockchain-based digital tokens, potentially enabling new trading and settlement arrangements.

Van Hollen argued that the exemptions could create a parallel stock market with fewer investor protections. His letter described the potential outcome as a “shadow stock market” operating outside safeguards intended to support fair pricing, market transparency and orderly trading.

The lawmakers specifically questioned exemptions from certain Regulation National Market System (Regulation NMS) requirements. These rules help maintain transparency across U.S. equity markets by addressing issues such as displaying competitive prices and reporting trades.

They also raised concerns about fair access requirements and market surveillance. According to the letter, reduced oversight could make it harder to identify practices such as insider trading, market manipulation and pump-and-dump schemes.

Another concern involves liquidity fragmentation. If tokenized shares trade through automated market makers without being directly connected to prices available elsewhere, their trading activity could become disconnected from the underlying stock market. This could affect price discovery and create uncertainty for investors holding either tokenized or traditional shares.

The senators additionally questioned whether the exemption creates sufficient safeguards against illicit financial activity, particularly where trading participants and liquidity providers may operate outside some traditional securities-market intermediary requirements.

SEC Defends Tailored Approach to Crypto Regulation

Atkins has presented the SEC’s regulatory changes as part of a broader effort to modernize financial rules and encourage digital asset innovation in the United States.

When announcing Regulation Crypto Assets in August, the SEC chairman argued that existing securities rules were not designed to accommodate the structure of crypto markets. He said the previous approach had created unnecessary barriers to capital formation and encouraged some businesses to seek regulatory environments outside the United States.

SEC Chair Paul Atkins proposed crypto exemptions allowing startup offerings of up to $5 million and annual fundraising of up to $75 million. Source: Paul Barron via X

The proposed framework aims to provide clearer requirements for eligible crypto projects while retaining investor protections. The SEC has emphasized that issuers relying on the exemptions would remain subject to federal securities laws’ anti-fraud and anti-manipulation provisions.

The agency also maintains that the larger fundraising exemption includes financial disclosure and ongoing reporting requirements. Atkins described the framework as a “fit-for-purpose” approach intended to provide entrepreneurs with clearer fundraising pathways.

The SEC has presented a similar argument for its tokenized securities order. In his September statement, Atkins said the Innovation Exemption would provide temporary, conditional relief while allowing the agency to assess how tokenized equity markets develop.

The order includes several conditions. Eligible platforms must comply with applicable sanctions requirements, restrict trading to permitted participants and provide underlying stockholders with the same rights and privileges as traditional shareholders, including dividend and voting rights. Companies issuing the underlying shares must also have an opportunity to object to their securities being traded through a qualifying platform.

Atkins further stated that federal securities laws’ anti-fraud and anti-manipulation provisions would continue to apply in full to securities activities conducted through these markets.

Regulatory Debate Moves to Next Stage

The latest objections highlight the continuing disagreement over how the United States should regulate digital assets without restricting financial innovation or weakening established investor protections.

Warren’s letter focuses on the proposed crypto fundraising exemptions, disclosure standards, and the SEC’s authority to establish a separate regulatory framework. Van Hollen’s separate request addresses the treatment of blockchain-based stock trading platforms and the market protections that apply to traditional exchanges.

The timing also brings the issue into the SEC’s ongoing rulemaking process. The comment period for Regulation Crypto Assets closed on October 20, 2026, and the SEC’s public docket records the senators’ submission on November 24. As of November 26, the agency continues to list the measure as a proposed rule rather than an adopted regulation.

The dispute leaves the SEC facing competing demands: providing crypto businesses with clearer rules and more accessible fundraising options while maintaining consistent standards for disclosure, market integrity, and investor protection. Whether the agency revises its proposals or maintains its current approach could influence how crypto fundraising and tokenized securities markets develop under U.S. federal law.

title: MetaQuotes Is Building a Client Portal Into MetaTrader 5
summary:
MetaQuotes is building a browser-based client portal into MetaTrader 5, the company said today (Thursday). The server functions behind it ship in beta build 6360, which brokers are told to install on test servers only.
The portal would give traders one place to manage all their trading accounts, pas...
content:
2026-11-26T13:24:09.232+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 11:24 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • One client ID would open all of a trader's accounts, with no outside software for brokers to buy, it says.
  • The same test build links the Ultency matching engine to Binance and adds an audit report on dealer actions.

MetaQuotes is building a browser-based client portal into MetaTrader 5, the company said today (Thursday). The server functions behind it ship in beta build 6360, which brokers are told to install on test servers only.

The portal would give traders one place to manage all their trading accounts, passwords and one-time verification codes. That layer is sold to brokers by back-office vendors such as FXBO, B2Core, Skale and Leverate, which FinanceMagnates.com compared in a 2025 review of broker CRMs.

The portal is tied to MT5 , which handled 48% of retail CFD trading volume in the fourth quarter of 2025, against 36% for MT4 , FM Intelligence data show.

One Login for Every Account

The portal rests on a client record that a broker creates to group all of one trader's accounts. After a single login with that client ID, MetaTrader 5 adds every linked account and lets the trader switch between them without signing in again, according to the release notes.

Brokers "will not need to purchase third-party solutions," MetaQuotes said, adding that everything they need will sit inside the trading platform.

The step follows build 6030 in July, which introduced unified client accounts secured with passkeys. Build 6360 adds the server side: login through the client account, the account list, password changes and OTP handling. The portal itself is still in development.

MT5 also draws more web traffic than MT4 in Asia-Pacific. Its websites had 1.5 million organic visits there in the third quarter of 2026, about twice MT4's 709,700, FM Intelligence's platform comparison shows.

An Earlier Move Into Liquidity Bridges

MetaQuotes took a similar step with liquidity bridges. In December 2025 it priced its Ultency matching engine at $1 per $1 million traded, against monthly base fees of $1,500 to $7,000 that it said brokers paid for third-party liquidity bridges.

By April, more than 30 liquidity providers were available through Ultency. Build 6360 automates most of the setup when a broker connects a new provider, including the trading account and the configuration files.

Binance Link and a Dealer Audit Report

The other changes for brokers cover crypto liquidity and two new reports. The same build connects Ultency to Binance over the FIX protocol, the notes said. They did not say which Binance markets the link covers.

A new Manager Actions Audit report lists, from the trading server log, who changed or deleted trades, adjusted balances or took other dealer actions, and when. It also covers managers whose accounts have since been deleted.

A second report, Ultency Execution Time, splits liquidity orders into placement and fill and shows mean, median, 95th and 99th percentile times for each provider. Brokers such as Axi, which began rolling out the engine in October, can use it to compare their providers.

MetaQuotes also said it optimized quote delivery, network queues and log replication across its servers. Backup servers can now replicate logs of up to 16 GB, up from 3 GB. MetaQuotes said the final build will follow a public beta test.

title: Binance Hack Highlights Money Laundering Risks as FCA Plans Tighter DeFi Rules
summary:

content:
2026-11-26T12:43:05.396+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 10:43 GMT by Tareq Sikder

  • Last month’s $6.3B Binance hack raised concerns over stolen funds moving through DeFi protocols.
  • The regulator plans DeFi authorisation requirements amid concerns over fraud, money laundering and consumer protection.

The UK Financial Conduct Authority plans to proceed with tighter regulatory requirements for decentralised finance platforms, citing concerns over money laundering, fraud and consumer protection, the Financial Times reported today (Thursday).

The move comes as the FCA prepares its wider crypto regulatory framework. Earlier this week, the regulator outlined restrictions on crypto exchanges acting as market makers on their own platforms.

Coinbase also expanded its UK operations into stocks and derivatives after receiving FCA approval in July. In September, the FCA opened an authorisation window for crypto firms ahead of the new regulatory regime.

FCA Flags DeFi Risks After Binance Hack

Jane Moore, the FCA’s head of payments and digital assets, reportedly raised concerns about the speed and scale at which stolen funds can move through DeFi protocols. She said this could make it harder for authorities to freeze assets and prevent money laundering .

The reported plans follow the October 29 attack on Binance, in which approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen. Attackers linked to North Korea reportedly used decentralised protocols, including THORChain, to move the funds.

🚨UK FCA TO TIGHTEN DEFI RULES AFTER BINANCE HACK! The UK’s Financial Conduct Authority is moving ahead with authorization requirements for DeFi platforms under its upcoming crypto regime, according to the Financial Times. Officials pointed to the $6.3 billion @binance hack last month, where stolen funds were routed through decentralized protocols, as a key reason for a stricter approach than in the US or EU, citing elevated risks of fraud, scams, and money laundering plus limited consumer recovery options. The FCA has already consulted on how existing operational resilience and financial crime rules apply to DeFi, with final guidance expected next year ahead of the broader regime starting in October 2027.

— Crypto Banter (@crypto_banter) November 26, 2026

FCA Also Plans Rules for Tokenised Shares

The regulator is also reportedly considering requirements for all UK retail equity orders to be executed on regulated platforms. The proposed rules would cover tokenised stocks as well as conventional equity trades.

On October 21, the FCA launched two consultations covering guidance on DeFi and the scope of its wider crypto regulatory framework. Both consultations closed on November 18.

The regulator is expected to publish its final guidance in January 2027. The new crypto regulatory regime is scheduled to take effect on October 25, 2027.

title: Robinhood Must Fight Sports Betting Lawsuit in Court After Arbitration Bid Fails

content:
2026-11-26T12:31:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 10:31 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • A federal judge said customers agreed to arbitrate only disputes over CFTC-regulated contracts, which sports bets are not.
  • The parties have two weeks to say whether to pause the case until the Supreme Court acts on New Jersey's Kalshi petition.

Robinhood Markets (NASDAQ: HOOD) must face a proposed class action over its sports event contracts in court. A federal judge yesterday (Wednesday) rejected its bid to send most of the plaintiffs to arbitration.

U.S. District Judge Edward Chen of the Northern District of California ruled that the arbitration agreements customers signed cover disputes over contracts regulated by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC ). Sports bets fall outside them, he found.

The ruling keeps in open court a fight over a business that now earns Robinhood more than crypto trading. Event contracts brought in $173 million in the third quarter, or 12% of group net revenue by an FM Intelligence calculation.

The plaintiffs are seeking to recover customers' losses under state gambling laws. Robinhood customers traded a record 16.4 billion event contracts in the quarter, more than seven times as many as a year earlier.

Robinhood had asked Chen to send 10 of the 11 named plaintiffs in four consolidated cases to arbitration. The 11th, a Michigan resident, had declined the arbitration agreement.

What Customers Agreed to Arbitrate

Chen accepted that the 10 plaintiffs had agreed to arbitrate by clicking "Agree" when they opened accounts with Robinhood Derivatives, the subsidiary that handles the contracts. The dispute was over what that agreement covered.

He read it together with the futures client agreement and the arbitration code of the National Futures Association (NFA), which covers commodity futures disputes. Gambling falls outside what the CFTC regulates, he wrote.

Chen concluded that "what the parties agreed to arbitrate were disputes about contracts regulated by the CFTC."

Robinhood argued that deciding the scope question meant ruling on the merits, which belongs to an arbitrator. Chen said courts decide scope even when it overlaps with the merits, and the agreement had no clause handing that question to an arbitrator.

Appeals Courts Split on Sports Contracts

His reading leans on an appeals court split over whether sports contracts are federally regulated swaps or bets that states can police.

In April, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit sided 2-1 with Kalshi against New Jersey, which asked the Supreme Court in September to settle the conflict.

The Ninth Circuit went the other way in August, ruling unanimously in Nevada's case against Kalshi that its sports contracts carry the hallmarks of sports betting. The same day, it upheld rulings against Robinhood and Crypto.com in Nevada.

That decision, Chen wrote, "strongly suggests that Robinhood's sports event contracts are nothing more than sports bets."

Robinhood has also fought the states directly. Its derivatives arm sued Nevada and New Jersey gaming officials in August 2025 to block enforcement. In September, it agreed to stop offering sports contracts in Michigan while litigation there continues.

Chen also cited a Sixth Circuit ruling against Kalshi. That leaves two federal appeals courts, the Sixth and the Ninth, siding with the states on sports contracts and one, the Third, siding with the exchange.

Customers Say They Were Sold Bets as Investing

The plaintiffs, from states including California, New Jersey, New York and Michigan, allege Robinhood runs an unlicensed sports gambling program. They say it leads customers to believe they are investing on a federally regulated exchange.

Robinhood began offering sports contracts listed by Kalshi in March 2025 and charges a commission on each one, according to the complaint as summarized in the order. It has since rebranded MIAXdx as Rothera with Susquehanna to route part of that flow through its own venue.

The plaintiffs also allege customers could trade the contracts against margin on their securities portfolios. New Jersey, New York and Michigan let people recover money lost to illegal gambling under laws modeled on a 1710 British statute, the complaint says.

Robinhood has said that event contracts, unlike sports bets where a firm sets the line, trade in a marketplace where buyers and sellers set the price, according to the complaint.

The case is not the first of its kind. The Ho-Chunk Nation sued Kalshi and Robinhood in Wisconsin in 2025 under federal tribal gaming law.

Merits Still Open

Chen stressed that his order is not a ruling on the merits. In a footnote, he wrote that it is not clear the plaintiffs will prevail simply because the contracts are gambling contracts.

He did not rule on their other arguments, including that the arbitration agreements were unconscionable.

The parties must file a status report within two weeks on a schedule for an amended complaint and on whether to pause the case until the Supreme Court decides whether to hear New Jersey's petition.
