Mutsamudu, Comoros, November 26, 2026 – MEXC, a pioneer in 0-fee digital asset trading, has released trading data for its October listings. Three of the five new tokens with the highest Spot trading volume were AI projects. Among the 10 new tokens with the largest price gains, the average peak gain was 1,168%. The gainers spanned sectors including GameFi, AI, infrastructure, and memecoins.

October’s Spot trading volumes show how interest in AI translated into trading activity. AXIS, CLAUDIA, and DNA ranked first, second, and fourth, respectively, among the month’s new listings by Spot volume. The projects illustrate how quickly AI is finding uses across on-chain markets: AXIS focuses on collecting data for robot training; CLAUDIA offers tools for users and AI agents to issue and trade tokens; and NeoSoul, the project behind DNA, provides infrastructure for AI agents to execute trades, manage risk, and settle transactions.

October’s biggest price gains also came from a range of sectors and blockchain ecosystems. RT, a GameFi token, led with a peak gain of 4,588%, followed by MTO, an AI and GameFi project, at 2,010%. Other leading gainers included CENT, a public blockchain; IBVM, a Bitcoin Layer 2 project; and RITUAL, a Layer 1 network for AI. The rankings also included token launch platforms, AI agents, and memecoins.

Some new listings also introduced different ways to launch tokens. GANG, one of October’s top gainers, operates a token launch platform on BNB Chain that only AI agents can use to issue tokens.

Alongside its early-stage listings, MEXC offered users more ways to participate through its Airdrop+ events. The platform ran 19 events in October, up 27% from September, with a combined prize pool of more than $1 million. Events featured AI tokens including AXIS and DNA. The maximum individual reward in the DNA event was $100.

MEXC’s flagship events drew more than 270,000 registrations in total. Nearly 89,000 users participated in BTC Carnival and generated $3.3 billion in Futures trading volume. The event offered a BTC prize pool worth $500,000, with a grand prize of 1 BTC for one participant.

MEXC CEO Vugar Usi said, “Our October listings data show that AI agents and early-stage assets across blockchain ecosystems are becoming major themes in the market. We’ll continue to list new tokens across these ecosystems and offer 0-fee trading so users around the world can discover promising crypto assets earlier and act on opportunities with fewer barriers to trading.”

About MEXC

Founded in 2018, MEXC is a leading global multi-asset trading platform built as your 0-fee gateway to infinite opportunities. Serving users across 170+ markets, MEXC provides simple and efficient access to crypto, stocks, tokenized assets, derivatives, and a growing range of TradFi-linked opportunities through one account and one gateway.

With 0 trading fees, deep liquidity, broad asset coverage, and a high-performance trading experience, MEXC is designed for retail users who want to discover earlier, act faster, and trade with fewer barriers. As crypto and traditional finance continue to converge, MEXC is committed to making global opportunities more accessible, helping users trade freely and MEXCmize every opportunity.

title: Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Faces a 9% Jump at the Worst Possible Time for Miners
summary: Key takeaways Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to rise about 9% on November 27, from 134.82 trillion toward 147 trillion, reversing much of the 9.13% cut on November 14. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, a 9% increase cuts expected BTC output per unit of hashrate by roughly 8.3%. At about ...
content:
Key takeaways

  • Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to rise about 9% on November 27, from 134.82 trillion toward 147 trillion, reversing much of the 9.13% cut on November 14.
  • Under otherwise unchanged conditions, a 9% increase cuts expected BTC output per unit of hashrate by roughly 8.3%.
  • At about $28 per petahash per day, a fleet running at 20 J/TH and $0.05/kWh would see its electricity-adjusted margin fall from about $4 to under $2.
  • The effect is uneven: efficient operators with cheap power can absorb it, while older fleets may switch machines off.
  • Difficulty alone is not evidence of more miner selling; miner balances, exchange transfers and treasury disclosures are.

Bitcoin mining difficulty is on course to increase by approximately 9% at the next network adjustment, expected on November 27. The increase would reverse much of the relief miners received less than two weeks ago, leaving operators facing tougher competition for block rewards while Bitcoin trades well below its previous highs.

Current network estimates put mining difficulty at 134.82 trillion, following a 9.13% reduction on November 14. If the projected increase holds, difficulty will climb back toward 147 trillion.

For miners struggling to keep their machines profitable, the timing is hardly ideal. The electricity bill remains largely unchanged, but the same hardware could soon generate less Bitcoin.

Bitcoin Mining Difficulty Is Reversing November’s Relief

Bitcoin adjusts its mining difficulty every 2,016 blocks to maintain an average block production time of approximately ten minutes.

When blocks are produced too quickly, the network makes the mathematical conditions for discovering new blocks more demanding. When production slows, difficulty moves in the opposite direction.

The previous 9.13% reduction in Bitcoin mining difficulty gave active miners some breathing room. Operators could expect to earn more Bitcoin from the same amount of computing power, provided other conditions remained comparable.

That advantage now appears temporary.

The upcoming adjustment, expected at block 977,760, reflects a faster pace of block production during the current difficulty period.

A 9% increase in difficulty does not translate into an identical percentage reduction in mining revenue. Under otherwise unchanged conditions, expected Bitcoin production per unit of computing power would decline by approximately 8.3%.

Consider an operator whose machines currently generate 1 BTC over a given period. Following a 9% difficulty increase, the same machines would be expected to produce approximately 0.917 BTC over an equivalent period.

Nothing about the hardware needs to change for that reduction to occur. The network has simply raised the amount of work required to compete for its rewards.

The Real Problem Is What Miners Earn From Their Machines

Mining difficulty only tells part of the story.

A more useful measure of the industry’s financial condition is hashprice, which tracks the expected revenue generated by a given amount of computing power over a day.

Hashprice incorporates Bitcoin’s market value, network difficulty and transaction fee revenue. It provides a clearer indication of whether a miner’s hardware is generating enough income to justify keeping it switched on.

Recent network data from mining industry trackers puts daily hashprice at around $28 per petahash of computing power.

At that level, the economics can become uncomfortable surprisingly quickly.

Consider a hypothetical mining fleet with an energy efficiency of 20 joules per terahash and an electricity rate of $0.05 per kilowatt-hour.

Operating one petahash of computing power continuously would cost approximately $24 per day in electricity alone. Against $28 in gross daily mining revenue, that leaves just $4 before hosting, maintenance, cooling, financing and other expenses.

If difficulty rises by 9% while Bitcoin’s price and average fees per block remain unchanged, that daily revenue would fall to approximately $25.69. The remaining electricity-adjusted margin would shrink to less than $2.

The network adjustment is the same for everyone. Its financial consequences are not.

An operator with newer machines and inexpensive power may comfortably absorb the change. Another running older equipment could find that switching off part of its fleet makes more financial sense than continuing to mine.

Bitcoin Miners Are Already Rethinking Their Business Models

The industry’s response to difficult mining economics extends beyond upgrading machines or negotiating cheaper electricity.

Some established Bitcoin mining businesses are redirecting infrastructure toward artificial intelligence and high-performance computing.

Access to substantial electricity capacity, established data centers and existing infrastructure gives certain operators alternatives that smaller mining businesses may not have.

This does not mean Bitcoin mining is disappearing. The projected difficulty increase itself suggests that blocks are being produced faster than the protocol’s target rate during the current adjustment period.

But the growing divergence between mining operators deserves attention.

A Bitcoin mining facility with access to inexpensive energy and efficient equipment operates under a very different set of economic conditions from a business relying on expensive financing and aging machines.

Rising difficulty does not necessarily make the entire industry unprofitable. It makes the difference between efficient and inefficient operators harder to ignore.

Does Higher Mining Difficulty Mean More Bitcoin Selling?

The prospect of shrinking margins raises an obvious question for Bitcoin investors: will miners need to sell more BTC to finance their operations?

There is a plausible case for additional selling from businesses facing substantial operating expenses or debt repayments. Mining companies cannot generally settle their electricity bills with anticipated future Bitcoin rewards.

However, network difficulty alone provides no evidence that miners have increased their Bitcoin sales.

Some operators hold substantial treasury reserves. Others sell their production regularly, regardless of market conditions. Businesses can also reduce operating expenses, shut down inefficient equipment or obtain financing instead of liquidating additional holdings.

Actual miner balance data, exchange transfers and company treasury disclosures will provide more useful evidence than the difficulty adjustment itself.

The immediate development to watch is whether the estimated increase materializes at the next adjustment block. After that, hashprice and changes in network computing power will help reveal how operators are responding.

Bitcoin’s protocol is doing exactly what it was designed to do. It adjusts the competition for block rewards without considering whether individual mining businesses can afford to remain competitive.

The machines that become uneconomical have always been the operators’ problem, not the network’s.

content:
2026-11-26T11:30:00.000+02:00

Thursday, 26/11/2026 | 09:30 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Parents have opened more than 500,000 children's accounts with the neobroker since May 2025, it said.
  • Berlin will pay €10 a month per child from age six, and providers may charge at most 1% a year.

Trade Republic will charge no fees on Germany's state-funded pension accounts for children, the neobroker said yesterday (Wednesday). Parents will be able to open the accounts, known as Frühstartrente, in its app.

The program starts on January 1. Trade Republic said it will charge no custody fees, savings-plan costs or ETF product costs, the same terms it set for Germany's new adult pension accounts in October.

The Berlin-based company also said parents have opened more than 500,000 children's accounts with it since May 2025.

For brokers, the program creates accounts funded by the government rather than by the client. It pays €10 a month for every child aged six to 18, or €1,440 per child, starting with those born in 2020. The cost of eligible accounts is capped at 1% a year.

Adult Accounts Already Priced Below the Cap

"Even €10 a month can make an enormous difference over decades," Trade Republic co-founder Christian Hecker said in the statement.

The children's accounts follow a price contest over the adult pension accounts, which also start in January. About 14.1 million Germans aged 14 or older owned shares, equity funds or ETFs in 2025, FM Intelligence data show.

Brokers cut fees close to zero for a shot at the €240 billion held in the Riester plans the adult accounts replace. Scalable Capital charges no fund costs in year one and up to 0.15% a year after that. flatexDEGIRO caps them at 0.07%, and Deutsche Bank charges 0.28% after two years.

The children's product has fewer published prices. WirtschaftsWoche, a German business weekly, reported today (Thursday) that Trade Republic was the first provider to set out its terms. Scalable Capital says on its website it will offer the accounts as soon as the law allows, but lists no fees.

In an October review, comparison site depotkonto.de found that comdirect and Union Investment planned offers without naming costs. ING and Consorsbank were still assessing the product. Only certified accounts qualify for the state money, and none was certified at the time, the site said.

Trading Fees After the Order-Flow Ban

Since July, Trade Republic has routed orders across about 30 exchanges for a €1 fee. It made the change after Germany's exemption from the EU ban on payment for order flow expired.

Its latest accounts, for the year to September 2025, showed commission income of €732.6 million and a net profit of €232.7 million, almost seven times the year before.

Trading traffic from Germany fell in the third quarter. FX and CFD broker websites drew 7.6 million organic visits from the country, 33.2% fewer than in the second quarter, FM Intelligence's heat map shows.

The Bundesrat, Germany's upper house of parliament, approved the program on November 20. Parents may add up to €6,840 a year. Money for children with no account will be invested by the Deutsche Bundesbank and can be claimed until age 35.

title: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Committee, Heads to Floor
Rep. Nick Begich's bill to write the Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into law, with a 20-year ban on selling its bitcoin, is now eligible for a House floor vote.
This post Strategic Bitcoin Reserve Bill Clears House Co...
content:
A bill that would write the U.S. Strategic Bitcoin Reserve into federal law is now eligible for a vote on the House floor, after the House Financial Services Committee formally reported it on Tuesday.

The American Reserve Modernization Act of 2026, H.R. 8957, was filed with amendments as House Report 119-894 and placed on the Union Calendar as Calendar No. 789 on Nov. 24, according to congressional records. The committee had voted 28-21 to advance the bill at a Sept. 16 markup.

Rep. Nick Begich, an Alaska Republican, introduced the bill on May 21. It now lists 23 cosponsors, including Rep. Jared Golden, a Maine Democrat, with Reps. Byron Donalds and Maria Elvira Salazar of Florida added on Nov. 24.

What the amended bill does

The reported text directs the Treasury secretary to set up a Strategic Bitcoin Reserve and a separate Digital Asset Stockpile within 180 days of the law taking effect. Bitcoin owned by the federal government would move into the reserve, while other digital assets would go to the stockpile.

The centerpiece is a lock-up. Treasury would have to hold all bitcoin deposited in the reserve for at least 20 years after enactment, and during that period no reserve bitcoin could be “sold, swapped, auctioned, encumbered, or otherwise disposed of for any purpose.”

After the 20 years, the Treasury secretary could recommend selling up to 10% of the reserve in any two-year period. Two years before the holding period ends, Treasury would have to send Congress recommendations on whether to keep holding or begin a gradual release.

Federal agencies would have 60 days after enactment to give Treasury a full accounting of the bitcoin and other digital assets they hold or have seized. Until the reserve is set up, agencies could not sell those coins except for national security, when required by law or a court, or to return assets to crime victims.

The bill also creates a Proof of Reserve system. Treasury would publish an annual report on total holdings, transactions and control of private keys, checked by an independent auditor with expertise in cryptographic attestations, while the Government Accountability Office would provide oversight.

States could choose to store their own bitcoin in segregated accounts inside the federal reserve, keeping title to the coins and the right to withdraw them.

Changes from Begich’s original version

The committee rewrote the bill before reporting it. Begich’s introduced text asked Treasury and Commerce to study funding bitcoin purchases with surplus remittances from Federal Reserve Banks or a revaluation of the Fed’s gold certificates, as well as with tax payments, tariff revenue and gifts.

Those options are gone from the amended study, which now looks at swapping other digital assets in the stockpile, forfeitures and settlements, and partnerships with states or private entities. The amended version also states that nothing in the study authorizes borrowing, pledging government assets as collateral, new taxes or deficit spending to buy bitcoin.

The committee also amended the bill’s title to drop a reference to offsetting costs with Federal Reserve resources, and removed a section that would have required the Exchange Stabilization Fund to report its bitcoin holdings.

Bitcoin Magazine reported on the bill’s bipartisan debut in May and on the full text revealing the 20-year lock-up in June. The reserve itself already exists under Executive Order 14233, signed in March 2025, but an executive order can be reversed by a future president, which is why Begich and his cosponsors want it in statute.

Setting up the reserve has been slow. In July, a report said Treasury and Commerce were competing over who would control it.

Begich’s bill has not received a floor vote. If it passes the House, the Senate would still need to act before it could reach the president’s desk.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Geo – Protocols Are Not Companies
summary: Yaniv Tal is Founder and CEO of Geo, a network for organizing knowledge people can trust, built on a decentralized knowledge graph. He co-founded The Graph, the indexing protocol that became core web3 infrastructure, after arriving in crypto in 2017 from a background building developer tools, and sp...
content:
Skip to content

Yaniv Tal is Founder and CEO of Geo, a network for organizing knowledge people can trust, built on a decentralized knowledge graph. He co-founded The Graph, the indexing protocol that became core web3 infrastructure, after arriving in crypto in 2017 from a background building developer tools, and spun Geo out as its own company in 2022.

The link will open a new window. Click the menu and down arrow to download the file.

Why you should listen

Yaniv’s central argument is that crypto made a category error. When the industry was overfunded in 2017 and again in 2021, investors rightly demanded to see what their money had built, and the shift to fundamentals was healthy. The mistake, he says, was borrowing the fundamentals of companies. A company sells a product, protects a proprietary advantage and returns margin to shareholders. A protocol like Ethereum is closer to public infrastructure, and its job is to deliver the most benefit to its users, who are often its holders. He welcomes Vitalik Buterin’s recent call to value ETH as a store of value rather than a fee-burning token, and points out that Bitcoin was never valued on fees either.

From there Yaniv makes the case for a small number of crypto stores of value, not just one. He challenges the view that only Bitcoin qualifies, arguing that moving trillions of dollars into a young technology calls for some diversification, and that Ethereum’s ability to upgrade leaves it better placed for risks such as quantum computing. He ties demand for stores of value to the debt loads of fiat governments and sets a 100-year test: listed companies tend to last only a decade or two by his count, so lasting value has to come from networks with real utility and network effects. In his framing, Ethereum is a global system of digital property rights. He also describes the market as a barbell, with fee-maximizing infrastructure for banks at one end and valueless memecoins at the other, and says what’s missing is the middle: networks people hold because they believe they make the world better. Changing that, he argues, is up to VCs, the media and every token holder, because developers build what the market rewards.

The final stretch turns to Geo. Yaniv explains why knowledge needs to be structured as a graph to be composable, revisits the semantic web that the web’s original architects tried and failed to build, and argues that public blockchain infrastructure and cryptographic verification finally make it practical, especially as people want their AI agents to control their own data. He walks through Geo Debates, where users vote on contested questions from geopolitics to health and AI, and previews the second season of Geo’s curator program, in which participants add context, publish knowledge and fact-check claims. He describes the long-term vision as something like Reddit built on a shared knowledge graph, where communities can flag what was taken out of context and hold sources accountable.

title: Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypto Tax Data Sharing Starting in 2028
Switzerland approved 57 partner jurisdictions, including all EU states and the UK, for automatic crypto tax data exchanges under the OECD's CARF from 2028.
This post Switzerland Picks 57 Countries for Crypt...
content:
Switzerland’s Federal Council has approved 57 countries and territories with which the country plans to automatically share tax information on crypto users starting in 2028, extending its long-standing bank data exchange to bitcoin and other digital assets.

The list includes all European Union member states, the United Kingdom and various G20 countries, the State Secretariat for International Finance (SIF) said in a release on Wednesday. The exchange will run under the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development’s Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework, known as CARF.

With the decision, Switzerland intends to implement the crypto exchange at the same time as other global asset management centers, according to the release. The government did not name the 57 jurisdictions beyond those broad groups, and it did not publish the full list alongside the announcement.

Exchanges only with partners that qualify

Data will not flow to every name on the list. An exchange will take place only if a partner jurisdiction wants to swap information with Switzerland and meets the conditions of the OECD standard, in particular its requirements on confidentiality and data security.

Before any financial account or crypto data changes hands, the Federal Council will run a targeted check of whether each partner complies with OECD standards. It will rely on a review mechanism Parliament approved on Sept. 28, 2026, which covers both the older exchange of bank account data and the new crypto exchange.

The domestic legal basis for the crypto exchange took effect on Jan. 1, 2026. Earlier this month, though, the SIF said the framework could not be implemented before Jan. 1, 2027, because the partner list still needed approval and notifications had to go to the OECD. The rules do not apply this year.

The Council also approved Armenia and Rwanda as new partners for the exchange of financial account information, with first exchanges due in 2028, and signed off on two notifications needed to carry out the exchange. Both partner lists were broadly supported during public consultations in 2024 and 2025, the government said.

Down from 74 partners

The final list is shorter than first planned. In June 2025, the Federal Council proposed 74 countries relevant to the crypto market, including all EU states, the UK and most G20 members. That plan left out the United States and Saudi Arabia, and it targeted a 2026 start with first data exchanges in 2027.

Wednesday’s release did not say which countries were dropped or whether the U.S. is now on the list. The U.S. has committed to begin CARF exchanges by 2029, according to the OECD’s Global Forum, which lists Switzerland among 27 jurisdictions aiming for first exchanges by 2028.

That U.S. timeline is already shaping policy elsewhere. South Korea pushed its 22% crypto tax back to 2029 partly because it will not receive American crypto trading data until CARF exchanges with the U.S. begin that year. Officials said taxing earlier could put Korea’s domestic market at a disadvantage.

Switzerland’s decision lands as European governments debate how much they should know about crypto holders. On Tuesday, France’s Senate rejected a rule that would have forced bitcoin holders to declare self-custody wallets, while EU states began collecting crypto transaction data under the bloc’s DAC8 directive this year.

For Switzerland, CARF extends a system it already runs for bank accounts. The country has exchanged financial account information automatically under the OECD’s Common Reporting Standard since 2018, ending much of the secrecy once tied to Swiss banking. Its regulated crypto market keeps growing, with the country’s financial regulator clearing its first bitcoin ETF in October.

Under CARF, crypto service providers in Switzerland will have to collect information on users who are tax residents of activated partner jurisdictions and report it to Swiss tax authorities, which then pass it on to those partners once the exchange begins.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Passports, Bank Accounts and Wallet Addresses
Bithumb said a follow-up review found its October breach exposed more people and data, including passports and wallet addresses, and lasted about 15 days.
This post Bithumb Says October Hack Exposed Pas...
content:
South Korean crypto exchange Bithumb said Wednesday that an October hack of its internal systems exposed more people and far more personal data than it first disclosed, including passport numbers, bank account numbers and crypto wallet addresses.

The exchange also said the intruder had access for about 15 days before being shut out, not the roughly one hour it reported last month.

In an updated notice posted Nov. 25, Bithumb said a follow-up review of the breach of Daou Office, its internal mobile groupware system, turned up additional affected people and additional types of data. The company said the new findings stem from the same incident it disclosed on Oct. 29.

Bithumb breach ran for 15 days

Bithumb now says an unauthorized outside party accessed the groupware system from 1:49 p.m. on Oct. 12 to 3:22 p.m. on Oct. 27, Korea time, and took personal information and files stored there.

That is a sharp change from its first account. Bithumb had said the hack lasted about an hour, from 11:28 a.m. to 12:27 p.m. on Oct. 27, and that it detected the intrusion at 12:14 p.m. that day. The revised timeline means the attacker went unnoticed for more than two weeks.

Bithumb first reported that the data of 6,444 customers and 715 employees, or 7,159 people in total, had been exposed. It did not give an updated count on Wednesday. The notice lists customers, employees of partner companies and current and former staff among those affected.

Passports, bank accounts and wallet addresses

The list of exposed data now runs to 19 items. It includes member numbers, names, mobile numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, resident registration numbers, passport numbers and driver’s license numbers.

It also covers bank account numbers, home addresses, gender, nationality, copies of ID documents, occupations, employer names and work contact details, as well as transaction histories and wallet addresses. Bithumb said not every item applies to every person, and that affected users will be told individually by email and text message what was taken.

For crypto users, the wallet addresses and transaction records stand out. Paired with names and phone numbers, that kind of data can help scammers target people they know hold digital assets.

Bithumb said Daou Office is an internal business system separate from customer exchange accounts and asset data. It said it has found no sign that its exchange service systems or customer database were directly breached, and that it has stepped up real-time monitoring of unusual trades and withdrawals.

Bithumb promises compensation

The exchange said it blocked the attacker’s IP addresses, fixed the vulnerability behind the incident and is running a security review of all of its externally exposed services. It has also set up a dedicated support desk for victims that covers financial and legal counseling as well as compensation reviews.

“We will take responsibility for all harm confirmed to have resulted from this personal information breach and provide all necessary support and compensation to affected customers,” Bithumb said.

Bithumb warned users that it never asks for passwords, verification codes or OTP details by phone, text or messenger. It urged anyone who gets such a request to stop responding, confirm through its official app or customer center and report any financial losses to police.

The disclosure adds to a difficult year for the exchange. Bithumb mistakenly credited users with billions of dollars in bitcoin in February, and regulators fined it $24 million and imposed a six-month partial suspension in March over anti-money laundering violations.

It also comes as South Korea weighs new rules for crypto exchanges, including a 20% cap on ownership stakes. Brokerages including Mirae Asset Securities and Daishin Securities have also suffered a series of cyberattacks.

“We are thoroughly investigating the cause of the incident,” Bithumb said.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Crypto News Today: Bitcoin’s $58K Battle Intensifies as Ethereum Risks $1,237 and XRP Longs Slip Underwater
summary: Bitcoin is struggling near $58,000 as options-market positioning leaves little cushion, while Ethereum and XRP face renewed pressure around key on-chain cost-basis levels.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC ETH XRP

Bitcoin is struggling near $58,000 as options-market positioning leaves little cushion, while Ethereum and XRP face renewed pressure around key on-chain cost-basis levels.

The latest market signals point to growing stress across major cryptocurrencies, with Glassnode highlighting increased downside volatility, weakening US demand, and significant investor losses.

Bitcoin Price Today: $58K–$64K Gamma Zone Raises Volatility Risks

Bitcoin traded around $58,500–$59,000 on November 25, returning to levels last seen during its summer decline. The move has also pushed BTC below the lowest Fire Sale band on the Rainbow Chart version highlighted in recent market discussions. The chart uses logarithmic regression to compare Bitcoin’s historical closing prices with a long-term growth curve, dividing the results into colored bands that represent different market valuations.

Based on historical daily closes, the chart shows the price is now outside its full model range. Source: @Cryptoze/X

The unusual deviation raises questions about the model’s usefulness during the 2026 correction. However, the Rainbow Chart is a historical valuation reference rather than a predictive indicator. Its calculations also vary across providers, with different regression periods and band settings producing different classifications for the same Bitcoin price. Consequently, moving outside one chart’s modeled range does not necessarily invalidate the broader framework. Previous periods of deep undervaluation have preceded recoveries, but they have not reliably identified market bottoms.

Options positioning presents a more immediate concern. Glassnode’s November 24 Week The on-chain report identified a short gamma zone between $58,000 and $64,000, where dealer hedging could amplify Bitcoin’s price movements.

Bitcoin is trading in a $58K–$64K short-gamma zone, where options dealers’ hedging now amplifies price swings by selling dips and buying rallies. Source: Glassnode via X

When options dealers are short gamma, they generally need to sell Bitcoin as prices decline and buy as prices recover to maintain their hedges. This behavior can reinforce existing price movements rather than reduce volatility. Glassnode noted that the current trading range offers little support from dealer hedging, warning that a move starting within the zone could pick up speed.

The report also identified long gamma positioning between $56,000 and $58,000 and between $64,000 and $66,000. In those ranges, dealer hedging could help moderate price swings. However, Bitcoin’s recent decline has already weakened its nearby support structure. Glassnode reported that the $62,000–$66,000 support zone broke on November 19, followed by an intraday decline to approximately $55,300 on November 21.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Glassnode also highlighted weakening institutional demand from the United States. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded approximately $4.3 billion in net outflows over 20 trading days, while Coinbase spot traders remained net sellers over the previous 30 days. Meanwhile, Binance activity showed a more balanced relationship between buying and selling.

The report identified Bitcoin’s realized price near $53,200 as another important reference point. This metric represents the average price at which existing coins last moved on-chain. Glassnode noted that previous bear markets eventually pushed BTC below this level, although Bitcoin has not yet recorded a sustained move beneath it during the current downturn.

Ethereum Price Risks $1,237 as Cost-Basis Support Weakens

Ethereum faces a separate challenge as its price falls below a significant historical acquisition zone. On-chain analyst Ali Martinez highlighted a Glassnode cost-basis distribution chart showing approximately 1.14 million ETH acquired around $1,680.

Ethereum has fallen below the $1,680 cost-basis level, putting approximately 1.14 million ETH holders at risk of further losses and increasing downside pressure. Source: Ali Martinez via X

With ETH trading near $1,640 on November 25, the price has moved below that concentration. The development leaves a substantial group of holders facing unrealized losses and raises concerns about whether buyers will defend the lower price levels.

The distribution chart identifies relatively thinner supply concentration below $1,584, with the next notable clusters appearing around $1,237 and $1,089. Approximately 1.37 million ETH were acquired around $1,237, while another 968,000 ETH have a recorded acquisition level near $1,089.

These concentrations offer potential reference zones if selling pressure continues. However, cost-basis distribution does not measure available buy orders or guarantee that investors will defend a particular price. It reflects where existing holdings were acquired or last recorded at an average acquisition price, making it useful for understanding potential areas of investor reaction.

Ethereum (ETH) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

A decline toward $1,237 would represent a substantial extension of Ethereum’s current correction. Whether ETH reaches that level will depend on market demand, broader cryptocurrency sentiment, and the ability of buyers to stabilize prices above the nearer support areas.

Martinez included Ethereum in his broader “prepare for the worst” analysis covering Bitcoin and XRP. The assessment highlights how weakening market conditions are affecting the cost-basis positions of holders across multiple large-cap cryptocurrencies.

XRP Price Faces $0.84 Support as Long Positions Slip Underwater

XRP is also approaching an important on-chain support level as the broader cryptocurrency market remains under pressure. The token traded around $0.91–$0.92 on November 25, remaining above the $0.84 cost-basis zone highlighted by Martinez.

XRP faces immediate cost-basis support at $0.84, with potential downside targets at $0.62 and $0.36 if selling pressure intensifies. Source: Ali Martinez via X

According to the analyst’s Glassnode-based chart, approximately 833 million XRP were acquired around $0.84. A sustained move below this level could expose lower historical acquisition clusters around $0.62 and $0.36.

The chart identifies approximately 1.11 billion XRP around $0.62, followed by a substantially larger concentration of 6.57 billion XRP around $0.36. These levels could become relevant in a deeper correction, although the size of a cost-basis cluster does not establish that buyers will return at those prices.

Derivatives positioning adds another source of pressure. Coinbase Markets published a Glassnode chart on November 24 showing XRP’s net open positioning by average entry price. The largest concentration of net long positions was recorded around $0.982, while XRP’s spot price stood near $0.923.

XRP is trading 6% below the $0.982 entry level of its largest net-long cluster, leaving nearly all leveraged long positions underwater. Source: Coinbase Markets via X

The difference places the largest group of these positions approximately 6% below their average entry price. The distribution also indicates that nearly all the recorded net long notional sits above the prevailing spot price, leaving much of the positioning underwater.

This creates a difficult situation for traders holding bullish positions. Some may decide to maintain their exposure in anticipation of a recovery, while others could reduce positions to limit further losses. Additional selling or forced position closures could increase pressure if XRP loses nearby support.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The distinction between spot cost-basis levels and derivatives positioning is important. The $0.84 zone reflects an on-chain acquisition concentration, whereas the $0.982 level represents the average entry price of a significant group of outstanding net long positions. Together, they show pressure emerging across both spot holdings and speculative trading activity.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and XRP Face Mounting Market Pressure

The latest indicators reveal different but interconnected risks across the three cryptocurrencies. Bitcoin is contending with negative dealer gamma, weak US buying activity, and a breakdown of its previous support range. Ethereum is trading below a significant acquisition cluster, while XRP faces pressure from both underwater derivatives positions and declining on-chain support levels.

Glassnode’s November 24 report also identified elevated options-market bearishness, with puts changing hands at approximately 1.7 times the number of calls on a seven-day average. That represented the highest reading since June 2022. The report further noted that realized losses had climbed to their highest levels since the FTX collapse in November 2022.

These readings point to widespread investor stress, although they do not establish that the current correction has reached its final stage. Bitcoin’s ability to regain the $60,000 level, Ethereum’s response to its lower acquisition zones, and XRP’s defense of $0.84 remain important areas to monitor.

For now, the three assets are showing signs of weakening market confidence. A sustained recovery in demand could ease the pressure, but continued selling would leave their respective support structures exposed to further tests.

title: Ethereum (ETH) Price Prediction: $1,500 Make-or-Break Support Could Decide Between $2,000 Rally and Sub $1,000-Crash
summary: Ethereum (ETH) is approaching a critical $1,500 support zone as BlackRock selling and BitMine accumulation raise questions over a potential bottom or deeper breakdown.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: ETH

Ethereum (ETH) is approaching a critical $1,500 support zone as BlackRock selling and BitMine accumulation raise questions over a potential bottom or deeper breakdown.

Ethereum (ETH) recently traded near $1,675, with technical analysts identifying the $1,500-$1,600 region as the next major support zone. While a successful defense of this area could support a recovery toward $2,000, longer-term chart analysis identifies $1,383 as a critical structural support, below which the risk of a deeper correction toward $1,000 increases.

Ethereum Price Breakdown Puts $1,500 Back in Focus

Ethereum’s weekly structure has weakened considerably after losing the support that held through much of the second half of 2026. Crypto Patel highlights a confirmed break of structure, with ETH now trading around $1,690 and moving back toward the horizontal support near $1,504.

That level matters because it sits near the lows formed earlier this year. A successful defense would give Ethereum another chance to establish a larger double-bottom structure, but a clean weekly breakdown below $1,500 would leave far less support underneath.

ETH has already lost the recovery trend, and bulls now need the $1,500 region to hold before the market can start discussing another meaningful higher-timeframe rebound.

Ethereum is approaching the $1,500 support region after a confirmed weekly structure breakdown. Source: Crypto Patel via X.

Analyst Warns $1,383 As Key Support

The bearish case becomes more serious on Peter Brandt’s long-term weekly chart. Ethereum is still trading above the rising support line that has guided the larger structure since the 2022 lows, but price is now moving much closer to the area where that structure would begin to fail.

Ethereum remains above its long-term rising support, but Peter Brandt sees approximately $1,383 as the critical level bulls need to defend. Source: Peter Brandt via X.

Brandt identifies approximately $1,383 as the critical level beneath the market. If ETH cannot remain above that region, the higher-timeframe structure would weaken considerably, and the risk of a move below $1,000 would increase.

That gives the current $1,500-$1,600 region even more importance. Bulls still have some room to defend the broader trend, but another sharp move lower would bring Ethereum uncomfortably close to Brandt’s larger breakdown level.

BlackRock Sells as BitMine Keeps Buying the ETH Dip

Large investors are taking opposite sides of Ethereum’s latest decline. Whale Insider reports that BlackRock ETF clients sold approximately $90.54 million worth of ETH, keeping institutional flow pressure elevated while price moves deeper into the correction.

Meanwhile, BitMine is doing the opposite. In a post on X Cointelegraph reports that Tom Lee’s company purchased another 7,819 ETH, taking its total holdings to approximately 6.09 million ETH, or around 4.98% of Ethereum’s total supply. The company is continuing to add while ETH trades near some of its weakest levels of the year.

That split makes the current range more interesting. ETF clients appear to be reducing exposure as price falls, while BitMine is using the same weakness to increase an already enormous position. Neither side confirms where Ethereum will bottom, but the contrast shows that the selloff is not being treated the same way by every large market participant.

Contrary View: Recovery Opening Toward $2,000

Not every higher-timeframe view expects the decline to keep extending. PILTR’s roadmap treats the $1,500-$1,600 region as a potential base rather than the beginning of a much deeper breakdown, although the chart still allows for more volatility before buyers regain control.

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, a successful reaction from this zone could first bring $2,000 back into focus. If buyers continue rebuilding from there, the recovery path extends toward $2,500-$2,800, turning the current selloff into a potential accumulation phase rather than a complete structural failure.

That makes the reaction around $1,500-$1,600 particularly important. A strong defense would support PILTR’s recovery scenario, while another sustained breakdown would shift the balance back toward the deeper bearish levels highlighted by Brandt.

PILTR’s roadmap sees $1,500-$1,600 as a potential higher-timeframe base before a recovery toward $2,000 and eventually $2,500-$2,800. Source: PILTR via X.

Where Can ETH Price Finally Stabilize?

ETH price is reaching a stage of the correction where the behavior around the lows matters more than another single red candle. Several higher-timeframe views are now pointing toward the same broad $1,500-$1,600 region, making this the area where buyers have the best opportunity to slow the decline.

A bottom does not need to begin with an explosive recovery. What bulls first want to see is selling pressure losing momentum, repeated defense of the lows, and price gradually reclaiming territory instead of immediately making another lower low. That would suggest the market is starting to absorb the supply hitting it.

If that process develops, $1,800-$1,900 could become the first meaningful recovery area before attention moves back toward $2,000 and above. Until then, Ethereum is still searching for stability rather than showing a confirmed bottom.

Q4 2026: Capitulation or Bottom?

Brave New Coin’s price chart shows that ETH has surrendered almost its entire recovery from the June lows, falling from approximately $2,750 in September to $1,644. The formation of successive lower highs and lower lows throughout Q4 reflects persistent selling pressure, with the market now approaching the same $1,500–$1,600 region that supported its previous multi-month recovery.

Ethereum price is trading at around $1,653, down 3.18% in the last 24 hours. Source: Brave New Coin

For the broader Ethereum Price Prediction, the final weeks of Q4 could determine whether ETH establishes a larger double bottom or extends its bearish trend into 2027. A sustained defense of $1,500, followed by a recovery above $1,900–$2,000, would provide early evidence of structural improvement. However, losing the June lows would expose the critical $1,383 support, below which the risk of a deeper correction toward $1,000 increases considerably.
